questions_for_owner.question: Build order and fiat ownership: does ArdaNova own money in AND out (Stripe Checkout + Stripe Connect payouts, rewards as rows in ArdaNova's ledger, AZOA chain mint as a later anchor), or does the chain-first order stand (KMS custody -> AZOA fiat rail via fiat-sidecar -> payouts last)?
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: Every thesis moment (sponsor, get paid) is currently dead behind custody+KMS. Two contradictory fiat designs exist (ArdaNova direct-Stripe with tests vs AZOA fiat-sidecar with its own pricing). Whoever writes the next gateway picks one. Fiat-first is the only order in which a real user can sponsor and be paid before KMS procurement finishes; it also keeps valuation out of AZOA per the thesis boundary.
options: A. Chain-first as the RUNBOOK sequences it: KMS (D27) -> AZOA Fiat.USD rail via sidecar -> payouts; thesis moments ship last

B. Fiat-first: ArdaNova owns Stripe in+out (Connect code already exists in StripeService.cs:290-380); sponsor units and worker stake live in ArdaNova's TokenBalance ledger; AZOA settlement becomes an asynchronous anchor behind the same idempotency key; retire fiat-sidecar and fix RUNBOOK D9
C. Hybrid: AZOA ledger-of-record with a Fiat.USD IValueRailProvider that delegates to Stripe Connect (two half-builds pointing different ways today)
questions_for_owner.recommended: B now, with C as the post-custody upgrade. Record it in contract §3 and RUNBOOK D9/D11 in the same commit window.

questions_for_owner.question: Custody posture: who is the custodian of record (ArdaNova self-hosts AZOA on Railway, or consumes an Escherbridge-operated shared node), and what is the honest minimum custody bar for first real money — vendor KMS/HSM (D27 as written) or a capped pilot on an env-backed sign-only key handle with enforced float caps (D36's direction, made explicit)?
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: Contract §11.1 says ArdaNova owns no KMS; reality is the same owner deploys AZOA on Railway and no third-party node exists. D27 and D36 contradict each other. Until answered, walletReady can never be true outside Development+Simulated, and no chain-backed value can move. Also decides who is legally custodian of every 'managed payment account'.
options: Self-host + capped pilot: sign-only key handle (env-backed provider allowed), envelope-encrypted DEKs, per-user and total-float caps enforced in AllocationManager, HOLD on a platform holding wallet; vendor HSM before uncapped mainnet
Self-host + no real chain value until a vendor KMS/HSM signs (D27 literal); fiat-first path (Q1-B) carries all real value meanwhile
Contract a third-party node operator (none exists today)
questions_for_owner.recommended: Self-host + capped pilot, amend contract §11.1/§2 to name ArdaNova as operator/custodian, and reconcile D27/D36 in the RUNBOOK so the next session does not re-litigate. Under Q1-B this is not on the critical path for the first sponsorship.

questions_for_owner.question: KYC policy: must a $50 card sponsor pass government-ID KYC and hold a custodial wallet before any value moves (current, implicit), or is KYC tiered — sponsors below a cumulative de-minimis pay by card with AML screening only; document KYC required to RECEIVE value (bid accept / payout); no wallet requirement on fiat actions?
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: KYC-before-$50 is the largest thesis friction that is a policy, not a bug. It fell out of the contract's 'gate at value seams' being applied uniformly by AzoaValueEligibilityService (funder AND recipient at checkout; owner AND worker at bid-accept; assignee at task create). D9 explicitly wants a fiat-only persona who never sees a blockchain; ArdaNova's gate makes that persona impossible.
options: A. KYC + wallet for everyone before any value action (current code)
B. Tiered: sponsors under a threshold need identity-lite/AML only; recipients (owners, workers) need full KYC at accept or payout; wallet readiness only on chain-rail actions
C. Recipient-only: never KYC sponsors; KYC at first payout request
questions_for_owner.recommended: B, confirmed with counsel (sanctions screening generally cannot be tiered; document KYC can). Gate the worker at settlement, not assignment. Record in conductor/product.md.

questions_for_owner.question: Unit of ownership: what is a sponsor's stake and a worker's stake, concretely — (1) units in ArdaNova's TokenBalance ledger per ProjectTokenConfig (DB-only, chain anchor later), (2) units of one real per-project ASA held in an AZOA custodial wallet, or (3) the status-quo code path of a brand-new ASA per reward/settlement? And is ARDA a user-facing currency or an internal accounting unit?
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: Three incompatible representations coexist (equityReward, awardAmount, TokenAllocation) and AZOA's AllocationKind.Mint creates a fresh ASA per allocation — a sponsor with 12 pledges would hold 12 unrelated assets that cannot be summed, swapped, or paid out. ARDA has no genesis (no mint, circulating supply always 0) so every USD conversion/payout preview fails, yet the invest page teaches 'ARDA equivalent' to sponsors.
options: Stake = TokenBalance ledger units of the project token (off-chain now); one ASA per project minted later into a platform reserve with an AZOA 'IssueUnits' allocation kind; ARDA internal-only (or removed), users quoted in USD + ownership %
Stake = real per-project ASA from day one (needs custody, opt-in, HOLD, reserve wallet first)
Keep Mint-per-reward and stop calling it equity
questions_for_owner.recommended: Option 1. Collapse equityReward/awardAmount into one field that creates the TokenAllocation reservation at bid-accept from the contributor pool.

questions_for_owner.question: Reversibility and seizure: how are card chargebacks/refunds reconciled against issued stake, and may the platform claw back any asset it issued? Options couple: a hold window (stake frozen until the Stripe reversal window elapses) plus clawback only for fraud/disputes, or clawback on every platform-issued ASA, or platform absorbs disputes from reserve.
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: Both repos drop charge.refunded / charge.dispute.* on the floor (D10 money-printer). D19 sets the Algorand clawback address on ASAs the platform creates — if that covers equity tokens, 'real ownership' is conditional on the operator. Whichever is chosen changes what 'you own it' means to the user and must be stated in plain words ('rewards become yours after N days').
options: Hold window on TokenBalance/ASA (frozen until reversal window) + clawback as the exceptional fraud/dispute path, disclosed
Clawback on all platform-issued ASAs, disclosed as 'platform may reverse rewards'
Platform absorbs disputes from a treasury reserve; equity ASAs minted with clawback = zero address
questions_for_owner.recommended: Hold window + exceptional clawback, disclosed in user terms; equity ASAs keep clawback only while the hold window is open.

questions_for_owner.question: Governance franchise and vote of record: who gets a vote on a project decision — one verified human (AZOA D3, KYC per voter), one project member (ArdaNova today, credential-gated), or stake-weighted — and is ArdaNova's Postgres Vote table or AZOA's claim ledger the record?
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: Two complete governance stacks exist that never meet and encode different franchises; AZOA's is node-shaped (vote = execute an action DAG with the option baked into node config, electorate = tenant or whole node) and cannot serve a vote button without a new REST surface; ArdaNova's vote route requires a membership credential no route can issue. Lifting the AZOA gate as scoped ships a primitive no ArdaNova user can reach.
options: ArdaNova is the vote of record, one authenticated member one vote, weight derived server-side; AZOA governance stays gated; anchor tally hashes later (D42)
Hybrid: ArdaNova counts, AZOA IPersonUniquenessGate consulted per ballot for one-human-one-vote (needs a small AZOA REST route)
AZOA claim ledger is the record (needs consumer REST/SDK, project-scoped electorate — a new design)
questions_for_owner.recommended: Option 1 now, option 2 when Sybil pressure appears. Decide franchise before any adapter is written.

questions_for_owner.question: Community surface: the social feed was deliberately deleted (17ec01d, 'No infinite feed') but the entire posts stack (unauthenticated PostsController, 14 tRPC procedures, entities) survives unused. Delete it, or build the README's 'field notes / open questions' project-scoped stream on top of it?
questions_for_owner.why_blocking: The thesis says people 'ask the community'; today there is no community surface beyond per-project comment tabs. The posts REST surface is live on Railway with caller-supplied authorId and no visibility filter — it must be deleted or hardened before any UI touches it. Track 12 still says 'Wire dashboard feed' P0, contradicting the deletion.
options: Delete the posts stack (client endpoint + router + backend controller/service/entities); project workstream tabs are the only social surface
Keep posts as a project/guild-scoped 'field notes' stream (visibility PROJECT_MEMBERS), harden the controller, no global feed
Rebuild a global chronological feed (reverts 17ec01d)
questions_for_owner.recommended: Option 2 — matches README.md:48 and FRONTEND_EXPERIENCE.md:56 and reuses the orphaned stack; rewrite Track 12 accordingly.

plan.thesis_health: Far. The vocabulary is mostly right — a person signs in with Google, sees 'Account setup', 'Identity check', and 'Managed payment account', and never meets gas, chains, signing, or seed phrases on ArdaNova's screens — and the substrate underneath is careful (single custody chokepoint, fail-closed gates at both dispatch seams, idempotent allocations, honest 'unpriced' analytics). But no thesis moment works end to end in any non-development environment: account setup returns 409 (EnableCustodialAccounts=false, CustodyMode=Disabled, Kyc:Provider=unavailable); a project cannot be edited, published privately, illustrated, or found past the first 50; sponsorship checkout is unreachable by construction (the only settlement gateway is a Retry stub, no project ever gets an assetId, the settlement would mint 'USD' cents as a fresh ASA, and no intent can reach SETTLED); a worker cannot submit a bid from the client, an accepted agreement never advances, escrow is 501/503, the thesis-native off-chain distribute is 501 and admin-only, and payouts are refused at controller and service; voting is a browser alert or a credential nobody can issue; and 'where did the money go' is an admin-only page. Where the UI does function it teaches ARDA, project units, per-ARDA rates, Algorand addresses, transaction hashes, and a Pera/WalletConnect picker in the sidebar. The build order is inverted against the thesis — three chains and a bridge shipped fail-closed while fiat in/out does not exist — and the two repos carry contradictory docs (self-sovereign vs custodial, sidecar vs direct Stripe, a Sybil hole already fixed, tracks marked complete that are 501). The honest path is fiat-first: fix the words and docs, make identity real, finish the presentation product, put stake in ArdaNova's own ledger with Stripe in and Stripe Connect out, and let AZOA's chain become an invisible anchor only after custody is worth trusting. Waves 3, 5, 8 and 9 are each multi-session; roughly a quarter of engineering before a real sponsor can pay a real worker, and the seven owner questions must be answered before Wave 1 starts.

verticals.thesis_verdict: No — but not for the reason the census feared. The user-facing words are right (Google sign-in, "Account setup", "Identity check", "Managed payment account"; no seed phrase, no signing, no gas anywhere in ArdaNova's flow), and ArdaNova has de facto chosen the tenant-custodial model, which is the ONLY model compatible with the thesis. The dead-end is configuration and half-built plumbing: ArdaNova ships Azoa:EnableCustodialAccounts=false (appsettings.json:17-24, .env.example:62) so "Start account setup" returns Conflict "unavailable"; AZOA ships CustodyMode=Disabled with no KMS/HSM adapter (appsettings.json:204-208, TenantCustodialAccountManager.cs:507-508) so walletReady/ready can never be true outside Development+Simulated; Kyc:Provider=unavailable by default (appsettings.json:136-138) and the Identomat trust profile is empty (198-203). AzoaValueEligibilityService.RequireReadyAsync (uncommitted) then forbids every sponsor/pay action with "Complete your account setup". So today a non-crypto user hits an honest but permanent wall — nobody can sponsor or get paid in any non-dev environment. Two genuine crypto leaks remain in the UI: the Algorand walletAddress rendered on the account card (custodial-account-card.tsx:49-51,88-92) and a top-level "Wallets" nav item asking for a public wallet address with Pera/Defly/WalletConnect (app-sidebar.tsx:140, settings/wallets/page.tsx:32-99). Meanwhile the contract that both repos carry byte-identically still "locks" self-register/self-run with no tenant:provision — which the code has already abandoned, and which could never have served a non-crypto user because AZOA exposes no hosted-KYC route for a self user.

findings.title: Launch model already decided by code: tenant-custodial, contradicting the locked contract §11.2
findings.detail: The contract (identical in both repos — `diff -q` is silent) locks 'self-register + self-run … no fleet map, no tenant:provision' (§10 ArdaNova block, §11.2). ArdaNova's only live onboarding route is AzoaCustodialAccountController -> PUT /api/tenant/custodial-accounts/{user.id} with a CustodyApiKey that Infrastructure/Azoa/AGENTS.md:7-9 says carries exactly tenant:provision+wallet:manage+kyc:read+kyc:submit. The self-sovereign AzoaAvatarService is still DI-registered but has zero callers; AzoaAvatarController is 410 Gone. ArdaNova tracks.md:49 calls azoa-user-onboarding 'largely shipped' while the AZOA conformance plan item 'Reconcile the self-sovereign ArdaNova contract' is still [ ] (plan.md:10) and the spec explicitly says not to let 'an alias field or example curl command make that product decision implicitly' (spec.md:36-40). That is exactly what has happened. The self-sovereign path is also structurally incapable of serving the thesis: a self user would need an AZOA password or wallet-challenge login, and AZOA has no hosted-KYC begin route for self users (see next finding).

findings.title: Production onboarding dead-ends: ready can never be true outside Development+Simulated
findings.detail: AZOA capability derivation: walletProvisioningReady requires custodyAvailable, which is true ONLY when CustodyMode=DevelopmentOnly AND env Development AND Blockchain:Mode=Simulated AND a 32+ char key (TenantCustodialAccountManager.cs:88-103). Base config is CustodyMode=Disabled; KmsHsm resolves to 'No production KMS/HSM custody adapter is registered.' (507-508). Status therefore carries walletReady=false, ready=false (422-444). ArdaNova's uncommitted AzoaValueEligibilityService requires status.Ready && WalletReady && WalletId && WalletAddress (46-55) and every value controller (funding intents, task escrows, bids, swaps — the in-flight security files) calls it. On the ArdaNova side Azoa:EnableCustodialAccounts defaults false, binding DisabledAzoaCustodialAccountGateway, whose Ensure/Status return Conflict 'unavailable; no account or wallet was created.' Net effect: in every non-dev environment, 'Start account setup' fails and every sponsor/pay action is 403.
findings.recommended: Treat 'KMS/HSM custody adapter' (contract B3) as the single critical-path engineering item for launch; until then the honest UI copy already shipped ('funding, paid work, and rewards stay unavailable') is the product.
findings.thesis_impact: Every non-crypto user hits it: they cannot sponsor or get paid, full stop. The wall is worded well, but it is a wall.

findings.title: AZOA has no hosted-KYC entry point for a self-sovereign user; Identomat is reachable only through the tenant surface
findings.detail: IKycManager.BeginAsync (the hosted session admission that leads to Identomat /begin) is called from exactly one place: TenantCustodialAccountManager.BeginKycAsync. KycController exposes only /submit (HTTPS document references), /status, /status/summary, /{id}, /{id}/documents — no begin/session route. So the contract's 'self-run user' could only ever do manual document-reference KYC, which docs/TENANT-CUSTODIAL-ONBOARDING.md itself says is 'Development only; production-disabled'. This is the structural reason the code drifted to custodial and should be stated in the amended contract.

findings.title: Identomat is not enabled by default and requires a HUMAN first-party AZOA login by the tenant to select it
findings.detail: Node default Kyc:Provider=unavailable and the approval trust profile (PolicyVersion, AssuranceLevel, TrustedProviderKeys) is empty, so 'an available adapter alone cannot authorize value'. Identomat becomes the tenant's provider via PUT /api/tenant/kyc/provider, which is [Authorize(Policy="RecentFirstPartyLogin")] — an API key cannot call it; someone must log into AZOA AS the ArdaNova tenant user with a password/OAuth session. The tenant user was created how? TENANT-CUSTODIAL doc bootstrap creates the key for 'an existing tenant user' via an Operator JWT + RecentNodeOperatorSession. Nothing in either repo records who owns the ArdaNova tenant user's AZOA credential. Identomat also needs CompanyKey/ConfigId/CallbackApiKey deploy secrets and PersonKeySecret.
findings.recommended: Write the operator runbook step: create ArdaNova tenant user -> operator issues tenant key -> tenant logs in first-party and selects Identomat -> set trust profile env vars. Store the tenant user's credential in the deploy secret store.
findings.thesis_impact: Operational, not user-facing — but until done, 'Identity check' is 'Identity verification is not configured on this Azoa node yet.'

findings.title: Who operates the node? Contract §11.1 'shared/managed node, ArdaNova owns no B3' vs. Railway self-host reality
findings.detail: Contract §2 says custody follows the node operator; §11.1 locks 'ArdaNova integrates against a shared AZOA node; that operator custodies… ArdaNova owns no B3 (KMS)/P3'. But AZOA is deployed by the same owner on Railway project 'ardanova' (per project memory), the tenant-key bootstrap requires an AZOA node-operator session, and no third-party node exists. If ArdaNova self-hosts, the KMS/HSM adapter (finding 2) IS ArdaNova's launch blocker and the contract's ownership table is wrong.
options: Self-host: accept B3 KMS/HSM + fee-funding as ArdaNova-org obligations and amend §11.1
Contract a third-party node operator (none exists today)
findings.recommended: Self-host and amend §11.1; the KMS adapter then goes on ArdaNova's launch plan explicitly.
findings.thesis_impact: Determines who is legally custodian of the sponsor's 'managed payment account'.

findings.title: Two disjoint identity systems: AZOA's OAuth/register/wallet-auth never touch an ArdaNova person
findings.detail: A person authenticates only via ArdaNova's NextAuth Google (config.ts:7, 327-329; signin page; all /signup aliases redirect to it). The AZOA identity behind them is a tenant child with synthetic email `{seed}@onboard.azoa.local` and a throwaway BCrypt password (TenantManager.cs:116,126), keyed by externalSubject = ArdaNova user.id (AzoaCustodialAccountService.GetUserAndBindingAsync; gateway AccountPath). AZOA's D17/D18 Google/GitHub OAuth (ExternalAuthController, ExternalLoginService — no email auto-link, OAuth≠KYC), /api/user/register, and wallet-challenge login (WalletAuthController) serve only AZOA's own operator frontend. This is the correct outcome for the thesis but it is undocumented: README.md:108 advertises wallet-challenge self-sovereignty as the identity model. The `claim`/`claim-invite` migration path (WalletAuthController.cs:84-118) that would let a person later 'take ownership' of their child user has no ArdaNova caller (grep 'claim-invite' in ArdaNova backend -> none).
findings.recommended: State it in the contract: 'A consumer person never holds an AZOA credential; claim-to-self-sovereign is a future opt-in.' Keep claim endpoints but mark them unused by ArdaNova.
findings.thesis_impact: Positive for the thesis; document it so nobody 'fixes' it back to self-register.

findings.title: Dead-but-registered AzoaAvatarService would collide and leak PII if anyone re-wires it
findings.detail: AzoaAvatarService.EnsureAvatarAsync posts the ArdaNova user's REAL email plus username = email local-part to anonymous /api/user/register. AZOA's RegisterAsync enforces global-unique username and email by a full-table scan (UserManager.cs:35-41), so `john@a.com` and `john@b.com` collide on 'john', and any email already registered on the shared node fails 'account already exists'. It is registered in DI and its spec is still the track spec's 'Overview'. Delete it rather than let the next dev call it.
findings.recommended: Remove AzoaAvatarService, IAzoaAvatarNode, AzoaAvatarNodeAdapter, AzoaPublicNodeClient in the contract-amendment commit.
findings.thesis_impact: Latent; a non-crypto user would see an inexplicable 'username taken' if it ever ran.

findings.title: UserManager.RegisterAsync duplicate checks are O(n) full-table scans
findings.detail: Both the email and username uniqueness checks call _userStore.GetAllAsync and LINQ over every user. On a shared node this is per-registration cost that grows with the node's population and is racy (two concurrent registers with the same email both pass). Tenant child provisioning goes through TenantManager, not this path, so ArdaNova is unaffected today; AZOA's own frontend register and any future self-register consumer are.
findings.recommended: Replace with indexed lookups (SurrealDB unique index on email/username) before any public self-register is offered.
findings.thesis_impact: None for ArdaNova users today.

findings.title: Crypto concepts still leak into ArdaNova's UI: raw Algorand address on the account card, and a top-nav 'Wallets' page asking for Pera/Defly/WalletConnect addresses
findings.detail: custodial-account-card renders compactReference(status.walletAddress) under 'Managed payment account' — a 58-char Algorand address a sponsor has no use for. /settings/wallets is a first-class sidebar item ('Wallets') whose form says 'Enter a public wallet address' with provider PERA|DEFLY|WALLETCONNECT. components/azoa/AGENTS.md explicitly separates these as 'non-custodial references' needing signed ownership proof — i.e., a crypto-native feature exposed to everyone. Also, the value-gate failure message 'Complete your account setup' is returned even when AZOA is simply down (AzoaValueEligibilityService swallows exceptions as Forbidden, :31-40), so an outage reads as 'you didn't finish setup'.
findings.recommended: Hide walletAddress behind an 'advanced' disclosure; move /settings/wallets out of primary nav (opt-in for crypto-native users); distinguish 'service unavailable' from 'not ready' in the eligibility message.
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: the only places a social-democrat sponsor is asked to think about wallets.

findings.title: Identomat hosted flow has no return-to-ArdaNova redirect; user must manually poll
findings.detail: IdentomatBeginRequest sends only companyKey/configId/clientUserId — no return/redirect URL — and the vendor's RedirectUrl is handed back with ExpiresAt=null (KycManager substitutes now+SessionExpiryMinutes, so ArdaNova's ExpiresAt guard passes). ArdaNova opens it in a new tab and offers 'I'm done — check status'. The verdict arrives asynchronously via the anonymous callback (KycCallbackController -> secret check -> /result re-fetch -> CAS terminal write), so the tab the user returns to shows the old status until they click. There is no notification/webhook from AZOA to ArdaNova; ArdaNova learns only by GET status (which also silently rewrites verificationLevel).
findings.recommended: Check whether Identomat /begin supports a redirect/return parameter; otherwise add a status poll on window focus in the verification page.
findings.thesis_impact: Friction at the highest-intent moment (they came here to sponsor).

findings.title: AML screening non-clearance is deliberately silent — the user is stuck with no recourse path
findings.detail: After an APPROVED Identomat verdict, KycHostedSessionOutcomeHandler runs AML screening first; any decision other than NO_HIT keeps the value gate closed and the code comments 'an adverse AML finding is not something to tip off about'. Hit/manual-review bands are AZOA-operator thresholds (ScoreThreshold 80, AutoBlockScore 95, open BlockingTopics set, truncated search -> manual review). ArdaNova's four-state projection can only show Pending/Rejected; there is no operator queue surfaced in ArdaNova (admin/kyc says 'Authority moved to Azoa') and no support/appeal path for a false-positive sanctions-name match — which is common for ordinary people.
findings.recommended: Define the manual-review SLA and a user-facing 'under review, contact support' state that does not disclose the AML reason; make sure an AZOA operator actually watches the review queue.
findings.thesis_impact: A false-positive name match strands a legitimate sponsor indefinitely.

findings.title: KYC approvals expire — is a 30-day default re-verification cadence intended?
findings.detail: TENANT-CUSTODIAL doc: 'Kyc:SubmissionExpiryDays controls expiry and is clamped to 1-365 days. Approvals require an explicit future expiry. Expired… approvals fail the KYC gate and surface as Rejected.' Base config SubmissionExpiryDays=30. If the approval's expiry is derived from that value (medium confidence — I traced the session expiry but not the approval-expiry stamp), every user re-runs Identomat monthly, and AzoaCustodialAccountService.ProjectVerificationLevel silently demotes PRO->VERIFIED on the next status read. Separately, ArdaNova's legacy KycService.cs:186 can still set PRO — two writers to verificationLevel.
options: Approval validity = 12 months (typical), session validity = 30 minutes
Keep 30 days and accept monthly re-verification

findings.title: No first-run onboarding: account setup is discovered only when the user tries to sponsor or post paid roles

The custodial 'account setup' surfaces only via the gates on invest and create-project pages, which link to /settings/verification?returnTo=…. That is a defensible lazy-KYC design (drafts/collaboration continue while setup pends, per components/azoa/AGENTS.md), but it means the Identomat interruption lands at checkout. findings.recommended: Add a soft 'Finish account setup' prompt on the dashboard after first sign-in so the identity check happens before intent, not during it.
findings.thesis_impact: Friction, not a crypto concept.

findings.title: ArdaNova User.azoaAvatarId is a UNIQUE index on the AZOA child-user id; claim/re-provision edge cases will violate it
findings.detail: User.cs:11 `[Index(nameof(azoaAvatarId), IsUnique = true)]`. TENANT-CUSTODIAL doc says user claim clears OwnerTenantId but retries resolve 'the immutable tenant-partitioned user id'; ArdaNova's StableReferenceError refuses a different avatar/wallet id for an existing binding (Conflict) and never clears the old one. If an AZOA node is ever rebuilt/re-namespaced (dev volume wipes are routine per memory), every ArdaNova user is permanently Conflict-locked until the column is nulled by hand. Also the column noun 'avatar' is intentionally unchanged (RUNBOOK §4) — correct per the rename policy, but the wire field is `userId` pinned via [JsonPropertyName].
findings.recommended: Add an operator-only 'unbind AZOA account' admin action (audited) for node-rebuild recovery.
findings.thesis_impact: Dev/ops only, unless a production node is ever re-seeded.

findings.recommended: Wire getUploadUrls into the wizard's Basic Info step, persist returned bucket paths as a JSON array (not comma names), render a media strip in the detail header and OverviewTab.

findings.title: description is silently overwritten with the solution text; server search only indexes title/description/tags

(:503). findings.title: Should a presented problem/solution live in AZOA at all (Project holon), or stay ArdaNova-only?
findings.detail: Today the Project row in ArdaNova Postgres is the only record; AZOA sees nothing until a FundingIntent/allocation happens. The contract sketches a Project holon created at publish (contract:186) and holon-state gate predicates reading holon.<projectId>.status (contract:279-282), which would make project identity portable and let AZOA gates read lifecycle directly — but it doubles the write path and gives every project an AZOA-side id that must never surface to the user. Contract:71 simultaneously says Domain lifecycle = Consumer-owned. Only the owner can pick.
options: ArdaNova-only: Project row is truth; AZOA learns of a project only through allocation/funding-intent calls (status quo, consistent with contract:71)
Mirror at publish via the authored lifecycle action (HolonCreate → Emit) so gates can read holon state; holon id stored on Project and never shown to users
Mirror only at FUNDED, when a ProjectShare token is created and a holon is needed to anchor it
findings.recommended: Option 1 now; revisit as option 3 when the funding flip lands. Option 2 adds a second source of truth for text a user edits often.
findings.thesis_impact: None visible to a non-crypto user under any option provided holon ids stay internal; option 2 raises the risk of a 'holon' or 'DappDevelop key' concept leaking into ArdaNova error messages.

findings.title: The create wizard front-loads an account-setup / identity-check status panel before the user has typed a word

The sidebar still labels /settings/wallets as 'Wallets' (app-sidebar.tsx:140).

Separately, /studio (Nova Studio: Draft/Review/Present/Rehearse) persists only to sessionStorage (studio/page.tsx:271,319) and labels itself 'Interface preview' (:534); there is no path from a Studio draft or 'Presentation outline' into the project record, so the clarity tooling advertised on the home page (page.tsx:63-80) does not feed the presentation surface.

verticals.thesis_verdict: Partly. The text core works and is thesis-clean: a person with no crypto knowledge can sign in, fill Problem / Proposed solution / audience / impact / timeline in a five-step wizard (no wallet, address, gas, or signing language anywhere on the path; draft creation is deliberately NOT KYC-gated), and the project appears on /projects with a Problem/Proposed-solution card and a detail page with an Overview tab. AZOA is completely uninvolved in this feature — the 'Project holon' in the integration contract is an authored-but-never-run definition. But as a PRESENTATION product it is thin and broken for every user, not just crypto-naive ones: the project can never be edited (no route, dead form), never published (no UI caller; every DRAFT — including partial-failure recovery drafts — is already public), carries no media (upload plumbing exists on both sides and is wired to nothing), duplicates the solution as the description, is discoverable only through a client-side filter over the first 50 records, and has no social/community surface at all — the feed was intentionally deleted in 17ec01d while a fully unauthenticated posts REST surface was left running on the backend. Verdict: a non-crypto user can present a problem today; they cannot revise it, illustrate it, control when it goes public, or be found once the community passes 50 projects.

findings.title: Funding checkout is structurally unreachable — no settlement gateway exists, so IsReady is always false
findings.detail: FundingIntentService.CreateCheckoutAsync returns Conflict when !_settlementReadiness.IsReady. AzoaFundingSettlementReadiness.IsReady requires `_gateway is ISelectedNodeSettlementCapability` plus attestation flags, but the ONLY registered IAzoaSettlementGateway is DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway, which does not implement that interface and returns Retry("AZOA_SETTLEMENT_DISPATCH_DISABLED") for both Dispatch and Reconcile. `Azoa:EnableFundingCheckout` is false in appsettings and, even flipped, cannot make IsReady true. findings.title: Chargebacks and refunds are silently discarded on BOTH sides; the D10 money-printer is unbuilt
findings.detail: ArdaNova's StripeWebhookController.DispatchAsync handles payment_intent.succeeded / payment_failed / transfer.reversed / transfer.updated; `charge.refunded`, `charge.dispute.created`, `charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn` hit `default: break` and are then MarkCompleted — the inbox records them as processed and drops them. FundingIntentStatus has no REVERSED/DISPUTED/CLAWED_BACK state and EconomicSettlementKind has no reversal kind. On the AZOA side the SDK orchestrator ignores every event except checkout.session.completed, and AZOA has no fungible clawback/compensation primitive (only soulbound-credential clawback in CredentialManager). Because AZOA mints a custodial ASA to the sponsor (see next finding), a day-60 chargeback leaves the sponsor holding tokens while the platform refunds the card. AZOA's own RUNBOOK D10 names this and the 'sidecar forwards dispute events + AZOA ledger facts + compensation saga' remain unbuilt.
findings.thesis_impact: A sponsor who disputes a charge (or a fraudster) keeps ownership tokens; honest sponsors' cap table is diluted by phantom holders. Also: there is no sponsor-facing 'request a refund' flow at all.
findings.recommended: Add REVERSED/DISPUTED intent states + an ESCROW_REVERSAL/FUNDING_REVERSAL settlement kind written from charge.dispute.*/charge.refunded; hold allocated tokens frozen (defaultFrozen ASA or AZOA-side lock) for the reversibility window before they count in the cap table; AZOA needs a clawback allocation kind.

findings.title: The durable settlement carries USD, not project tokens — nobody converts, and ArdaNova's economics (valuation, treasury split) are not on the path
findings.detail: CreateFundingSettlement stamps assetCode = 'USD', amount = intent.amount (USD, scale 2); EconomicOutboxLeaseStore turns that into AzoaSettlementRequest(AssetCode 'USD', FixedScaleAmount in cents). The project token symbol/assetId live only inside the termsSnapshot JSON. The invest page shows an estimate of project units via exchange.getConversionPreview, but nothing on the durable path computes token units at settlement. The ONLY code that does the USD→token math (usd/valuationBase*totalSupply), credits TokenBalance, and runs TreasuryService.ProcessFundingInflowAsync is the legacy StripeService.HandlePaymentSucceededAsync — which has zero callers (dead). Result: even with a live gateway, AZOA would be asked to mint 'USD' base units, and the sponsor's ArdaNova portfolio (tokenBalances.getPortfolio) would never show the holding, and the project treasury never records the inflow.
findings.evidence: FundingIntentService.cs:408-428 (assetCode = currencyCode), :482-500 (termsSnapshot); ArdaNova.Infrastructure/Outbox/EconomicOutboxLeaseStore.cs:61-79; StripeService.cs:154-240 (dead: grep HandlePaymentSucceededAsync → only StripeService + interface); TreasuryController.cs:39-47 (only other caller, admin-only manual endpoint); ardanova-client/src/app/portfolio/page.tsx:76; invest/page.tsx:155-170
findings.thesis_impact: The core promise — 'back a project and own a stake' — has no ledger entry on either side. The sponsor sees 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' forever and an empty portfolio.
findings.recommended: Decide the unit of settlement at intent creation (lock token quantity in termsSnapshot from the same preview the sponsor accepted), store it as a typed field, credit ArdaNova's TokenBalance + treasury in the same transaction as SETTLED, and only then dispatch that token quantity to AZOA.

findings.title: AZOA 'Mint' allocation creates a brand-new ASA per settlement — it cannot give a sponsor units of the project's existing token
findings.detail: AllocationManager.MintAsync builds an NftMintRequest and a BlockchainOperation 'Mint'; BlockchainOperationManager.ExecuteMintAsync calls provider.MintAsync(tokenUri, amount, assetType, walletAddress), and AlgorandProvider.MintAsync is CreateAsaCoreAsync — an AssetCreate with total = net amount, unit name derived from assetType, wallet as creator. request.AssetId (the project's ASA id) is only carried as TokenId/TokenUri metadata. So each sponsorship would produce a fresh ASA named after the settlement (e.g. 'ArdaNova funding settlement for pi_...'), not units of ProjectTokenConfig.assetId. The only way to hand out units of an existing ASA is AllocationKind.Transfer with an AssetRecordId from the CALLER's (tenant's) wallet — which requires ArdaNova to custody the project's reserve in AZOA, and Transfer is denied outright whenever the node fee > 0. Whoever writes the real gateway is choosing between (a) one-ASA-per-sponsor, (b) tenant-held reserve + Transfer, (c) a new 'mint more of existing ASA' allocation kind in AZOA. That choice determines whether 'ownership' is real, fungible, and swappable.
findings.evidence: oasis-sleek/Managers/AllocationManager.cs:240-292 (Mint), :294-356 (Transfer requires AssetRecordId), :444-447 (Transfer fee denial); Managers/BlockchainOperationManager.cs:444-465; Providers/Blockchain/Algorand/AlgorandProvider.cs:490-511, :1150-1164; ArdaNova AzoaAllocationService.cs:88-99 (Kind: Mint, AssetId passed as metadata)
findings.thesis_impact: Sponsor ends up holding a token nobody else holds; cannot be swapped/pooled/counted on a cap table. Real ownership is the thesis benefit being promised.
options: (a) Keep Mint: one ASA per sponsorship — simplest, but ownership is non-fungible and cap-table math becomes off-chain fiction
(b) ArdaNova tenant wallet holds each project's reserve in AZOA and settles via Kind=Transfer (needs fee-funded treasury settlement to unblock the Transfer fee denial)
(c) Add an AZOA allocation kind 'IssueUnits' that transfers from the ASA reserve address the platform already controls (CreateAsaCoreAsync sets platform as reserve/manager)
findings.recommended: (c) — it matches the fact that AZOA is already the ASA manager/reserve for project tokens created through FungibleTokenManager, keeps ArdaNova out of custody, and stays exactly-once through the existing idempotency ledger.

findings.title: No code ever writes ProjectTokenConfig.assetId, yet checkout requires a 'verified asset id'
findings.detail: CreateCheckoutAsync rejects with 'Project token configuration requires a verified asset id before funding checkout' when config.assetId is blank, and the replay path re-validates it. Across ArdaNova.Application and ArdaNova.API the only references to ProjectTokenConfig.assetId are reads (FundingIntentService, contracts); ProjectTokenService.CreateConfigAsync never sets it, there is no DTO field for it, and no AZOA fungible-mint call populates it back. So every project is permanently in the 'no verified asset' state unless the DB is hand-edited. The project-token issuance leg (ArdaNova → AZOA FungibleTokenManager) that should produce this id is absent.
findings.evidence: FundingIntentService.cs:86-87, :320-325, :502-509; ArdaNova.Domain/Models/Entities/ProjectTokenConfig.cs:22; ProjectTokenService.cs:64-110 (no assetId); grep '\.assetId =' over Application/API → only MembershipCredentialServices
findings.thesis_impact: Founders cannot open funding at all; sponsors see 'Funding terms unavailable'.
findings.recommended: Build the issuance step: on gate → FUNDING, ArdaNova calls AZOA fungible-mint (AzoaNodeClient.PostAsync fungible path already exists at AzoaNodeClient.cs:65-70) and persists the returned assetId + scale.

findings.title: A funding intent can never reach SETTLED — the sponsor polls 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' forever
findings.detail: No code assigns FundingIntentStatus.SETTLED or PAYMENT_VERIFIED (the lifecycle skips DRAFT→AWAITING_PAYMENT→SETTLEMENT_PENDING and stops). Outbox finalization only advances EconomicSettlement to SUBMITTED on Accepted; nothing links a confirmed AZOA operation back to the intent. With the disabled gateway every dispatch returns Retry, backoff capped at 300s, forever — no attempt ceiling, no operator alert, no refund branch. The success page polls every 5s for any status with poll:true (SETTLEMENT_PENDING is poll:true) with no timeout.
findings.evidence: grep 'FundingIntentStatus.SETTLED' assignments → none; EconomicOutboxLeaseStore.cs:164 (Accepted → SUBMITTED only); EconomicOutboxDispatchService.cs:220-231; ardanova-client/src/lib/commerce/funding-intent-status.ts:26-31; invest/success/page.tsx:24-33
findings.thesis_impact: The sponsor's card is charged and the UI never confirms anything. That is the single most trust-destroying experience for a non-crypto backer.
findings.recommended: Add the confirmed-operation → settlement SETTLED → intent SETTLED transition (receipt reconcile via /api/allocation/receipt), an attempt ceiling that flips to FAILED + auto-refund, and a 'we'll email you' terminal state on the success page.

findings.title: Stale docs: AZOA RUNBOOK says fiat reaches Stripe ONLY via fiat-sidecar; ArdaNova talks to Stripe directly and never references the sidecar
findings.detail: oasis-sleek/conductor/RUNBOOK.md D9 states 'Fiat reaches Stripe only through fiat-sidecar/, never directly (integration contract §3)'. The contract §3 actually says the opposite ('AZOA holds no payment-provider secret — webhook verification is the consumer's job'), and ArdaNova creates Checkout Sessions and verifies webhooks itself. The sidecar is an orphan: zero references from any ArdaNova file, only an opt-in `profiles: ["fiat"]` service in AZOA's docker-compose.dev.yml with placeholder secrets, no Railway service under deploy/railway, and it still imports the renamed package as '@azoa/wallet-sdk' (file:../sdk/azoa-wallet whose package name is now 'azoa-sdk'). It also embeds its own economics (TOKENS_PER_CENT price schedule), contradicting 'ArdaNova owns ALL domain economics'.

findings.thesis_impact: Two competing fiat designs means the next engineer may build the wrong one; the sidecar path would put pricing in AZOA, violating the substrate boundary.
findings.recommended: Retire fiat-sidecar (or demote it to 'reference for other tenants') and fix RUNBOOK D9; ArdaNova's direct-Stripe + outbox design is the one with tests and a KYC-aware dispatch loop.

findings.title: Which fiat transport is canonical, and who holds the Stripe account: ArdaNova, the AZOA node operator, or a sidecar per tenant?
findings.detail: Code has ArdaNova owning Stripe keys, webhooks, and the settlement outbox (consumer-side), with AZOA receiving already-decided amounts — consistent with the thesis. AZOA docs and the shipped fiat-sidecar assume AZOA/operator-side Stripe with per-cent token pricing. The answer also decides where reversal handling lives and whether ArdaNova needs `tenant:provision` for a custodial fleet (it currently does: the allocation is tenant-driven with act_as_tenant consent).

findings.thesis_impact: Determines whether a sponsor's money and tokens are reconciled by one party or split across two ledgers with no shared reversal story.
options: ArdaNova-owned Stripe + outbox → AZOA allocation (current code); delete sidecar
AZOA operator-owned sidecar; ArdaNova only posts intents (requires moving valuation into AZOA — violates thesis boundary)

Stripe Connect: ArdaNova is platform, project owners are connected accounts (PayoutService already has CreateConnectedAccountAsync) — sponsors pay the project directly, ArdaNova takes an application fee
findings.recommended: Option 1 for collection now; evaluate option 3 for the owner-side payout leg since StripeService already has Connect scaffolding (CreateConnectedAccountAsync, CreatePayoutTransferAsync).

findings.title: Both the sponsor AND the project owner must be KYC-Approved with a provisioned wallet before a $100 sponsorship can even start checkout
findings.detail: CreateCheckoutAsync calls RequireReadyAsync for the funder and, unless self-funding, for project.createdById; AzoaValueEligibilityService.IsReadyForValueAction requires Ready && IdentityReady && KycStatus==Approved && WalletReady && walletAddress. The dispatcher re-checks both at every dispatch attempt and parks the money on Retry if either lapses (no refund branch). AZOA enforces its own fail-closed gate again (ValueAccessService → KycGateService). This is being decided by whoever coded first; the product has no threshold (e.g. KYC only above $X, or KYC-lite for sponsors vs full for recipients).
findings.thesis_impact: A social-democrat crowd backing a neighbour's project with $50 is sent to 'Identity verification' with a document-upload provider first. This is the biggest friction point that is NOT a bug.
options: Keep full KYC for everyone (current)
Tiered: sponsor KYC only above a cumulative threshold; recipient KYC always (money-out side)
Defer sponsor KYC: accept payment, hold tokens frozen until KYC completes (also solves the chargeback window)
findings.recommended: Tiered + deferred: collect the payment, hold the allocation frozen until both KYC and the reversal window clear. The outbox already models 'pending' well; add a hold state instead of a Retry loop.

findings.title: Stripe SuccessUrl is one static config value, but the return page is per-project and keyed by slug in sessionStorage
findings.detail: StripeCheckoutGateway reads Stripe:SuccessUrl once and uses it for every session; there is no slug or intentId in the URL or in StripeCheckoutRequest. The client stores the intentId under `ardanova:funding-intent:${slug}` and only /projects/[slug]/invest/success reads it. Unless SuccessUrl happens to point at exactly that project's page, the sponsor lands on a page that cannot find the intent and shows 'FUNDING STATUS UNAVAILABLE'. Also appsettings.json has no Stripe section, so RequiredUrl throws — AFTER the FundingIntent row has been committed as DRAFT (lines 139-144), leaving orphan intents whose idempotency key is now burned for that (amount, config) tuple.

findings.thesis_impact: Every sponsor returning from Stripe hits it.
findings.recommended: Build success/cancel URLs per intent (`/projects/{slug}/invest/success?intent={id}` with the server as source of truth) and validate Stripe config at startup, not at first checkout.

findings.title: AZOA silently shaves a node fee off the 'already-decided' amount, and any Transfer fee > 0 hard-denies refunds
findings.detail: AllocationManager quotes NodeFeeScheduleManager, mints feeQuote.NetAmount, and stamps Gross/Fee/Net into metadata; ArdaNova's settlement amount is gross and ArdaNova never reads the fee back. For Kind=Transfer any fee > 0 returns 'Transfer node fees require on-chain treasury settlement, which is not configured; allocation denied' — and ArdaNova's RefundAsync uses Kind=Transfer. Default schedule is version 0 (zero fees) so this is latent until an operator sets fees.
findings.thesis_impact: Sponsor sees fewer units than the invest-page preview promised, with no explanation; escrow refunds break the day a fee is configured.
findings.recommended: ArdaNova must quote AZOA's fee before locking terms (or the node must expose 'fee: 0 for tenant X'); surface the fee on the review step.

findings.title: Two idempotency-key conventions for the same funding event
findings.detail: Contract §6 and AzoaAllocationService use the Stripe PaymentIntent id verbatim (then avatar-prefixed `{avatarId}:{key}`), while the durable outbox path uses settlement.idempotencyKey = `funding-intent:{intentId}` and would pass that to a real gateway. A future gateway that reconciles via /api/allocation/receipt must use whichever key was sent; mixing them defeats replay detection.
findings.thesis_impact: Indirect: a double-mint on webhook redelivery would give one sponsor two allocations.
findings.recommended: Standardise on `{avatarId}:funding-intent:{intentId}` (intent-bound, recipient-bound) and delete AllocationKeys.FundingSettlement.

findings.title: Crypto leaks in sponsor-facing copy are small but present
findings.detail: The wording is mostly thesis-compliant ('Managed payment account', 'Identity check', 'project units'), and no gas, chain, seed phrase, or signing is ever shown. Leaks: the custodial-account card prints the truncated Algorand wallet address as the 'Managed payment account' detail; the verification page says 'Wallet custody may be configured independently'; the success page uses a Wallet icon labelled 'VIEW MY PORTFOLIO'; checkout failure strings are operator-facing ('selected AZOA node', 'attested settlement dispatch and reconciliation', 'node fee quote…') and are passed straight to the UI via result.Error.
findings.thesis_impact: Minor; the 409/500 strings are the worst offenders because they are the ones a sponsor actually sees today.
findings.recommended: Drop the address from the card (show 'Ready'), map server error codes to plain-language copy client-side.

verticals.thesis_verdict: No. A non-crypto sponsor cannot complete a sponsorship today, and the failure has nothing to do with crypto literacy — the path is cut in four places before the UX even gets a chance: (1) checkout always 409s because the only settlement gateway is a Disabled stub that can never satisfy the readiness port; (2) no project can ever have the 'verified asset id' checkout demands because nothing writes it; (3) if both were fixed, the settlement would ask AZOA to mint 'USD' cents as a brand-new ASA rather than units of the project token, and ArdaNova's own ledger (TokenBalance, treasury) would still record nothing — the only code with the valuation math is a dead legacy Stripe handler; (4) a funding intent has no transition to SETTLED, so the sponsor's card is charged and the return page polls 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' forever. On chargebacks: both sides drop charge.dispute.* and charge.refunded on the floor — the intent, the settlement, and the AZOA allocation have no reversal state or clawback, so a disputed payment would leave the sponsor holding tokens (the RUNBOOK D10 money-printer, still open). What IS thesis-aligned: the sponsor never sees gas, chains, signing or seed phrases; the copy says 'Managed payment account' and 'Identity check'; ArdaNova correctly owns Stripe and passes AZOA an opaque amount. What is being decided implicitly and needs the owner: full KYC for sponsor AND founder before a single dollar (with the money parked on infinite Retry if either lapses), and which of two contradictory fiat designs (ArdaNova-direct vs AZOA fiat-sidecar) is canonical — the docs say sidecar, the working code says direct.

findings.title: No path pays a worker today — every settlement hop dead-ends
findings.detail: Trace of the designed flow (gated-commerce spec: bid → accept → escrow funded → run → release → settled) against code: (1) accept creates a ProjectTask + TaskCommerceAgreement in ACCEPTED and does nothing else — ACCEPTED is the only status ever written, the ESCROW_FUNDED…SETTLED enum members are never assigned anywhere; (2) marking a task COMPLETED only stamps completedAt; (3) completing a bid only flips BidStatus; (4) AzoaAllocationService.AllocateRewardAsync — the exactly-once money path — has zero callers; (5) the only EconomicSettlement kind ever created is FUNDING_ALLOCATION; (6) IAzoaSettlementGateway is DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway (returns Retry forever) and the outbox worker defaults off; (7) the Task Bounty action DAG exists but no controller publishes or signals it. tracks.md:52 already admits 'no production trigger dispatches it yet'.

findings.title: D14 is still true: nothing in either repo can HOLD value, and the in-flight hardening proves it by switching the paper escrow off
findings.detail: AZOA has no hold primitive: the ActionNodeType catalog has no Escrow/Hold, AllocationKind is Mint|Transfer only, and IValueRailProvider.cs:40 refers to 'Escrow/release logic' that does not exist. ArdaNova's TaskEscrow is a DB row whose fund/release/refund evidence is a client-typed txHash string. At HEAD, ReleaseAsync/RefundAsync flipped status to RELEASED/REFUNDED on whatever txHash the funder typed (the removed bodies are visible in the working-tree diff) — the same fabricated-success class the AZOA runbook flags three times. The uncommitted hardening replaces both with a 503 and Create with a 501. So: 'layer escrow on existing primitives' remains unbuildable exactly as D14 says; the closest thing to a hold is a DB counter (ProjectTokenConfig.allocatedSupply) that AcceptBidAsync does not even decrement.

findings.title: AZOA 'reward' = mint a brand-new ASA, not units of the project's stake — and the spec says Transfer
findings.detail: AllocateRewardAsync sends kind=Mint. On AZOA, AllocationKind.Mint builds an NftMintRequest and drives 'Mint' through the provider, and AlgorandProvider.MintAsync is CreateAsaCoreAsync: a NEW asset with total = amount, decimals 0, name = the request name ('ArdaNova task reward for {taskId}'). A worker settled this way would hold a fresh, unrelated asset — not equity in the project. The treasury-reward spec's own table says escrow release should be kind: Transfer (spec.md:77), so code and spec disagree. Transfer cannot work either: it needs an AssetRecordId of an existing AZOA-held asset, and the project token ASA is never minted (CreateFungibleASAAsync has no callers; ProjectTokenConfig.assetId is left null by CreateConfigAsync). Whoever writes the first caller of AllocateRewardAsync decides what 'stake' means by accident.

findings.thesis_impact: Invisible to the user until they look at their holdings and find a token that is not the project's.
options: Off-chain project-token ledger only (TokenBalance) — no AZOA call for worker pay in v1
Mint the per-project ASA once (FungibleTokenCreate / fungible-mint) and settle worker pay as Transfer of that asset from a project treasury wallet
Keep Mint-per-reward and accept that stake is not fungible with the project token
findings.recommended: Option 1 now (matches 09-tokenomics 'all blockchain operations are abstracted from users'), with option 2 as the chain-backed follow-up; rename/retire AllocateRewardAsync's Mint kind so nobody wires it as-is.

findings.title: The one path that actually expresses 'worker receives project stake' is an off-chain ledger credit, and it is 501
findings.detail: ProjectTokenService.DistributeAsync moves a TokenAllocation RESERVED→DISTRIBUTED and credits ITokenBalanceService for the recipient — a pure DB internal economy in the project's own unit, exactly the thesis' 'tokens support an internal economy'. The worker-facing read side exists (portfolio page reads token balances). But the route returns 501 at HEAD, the allocate/pbi route that creates the RESERVED row is 501 in the in-flight diff, and all of them are AdminApiKey-only — a project owner cannot reach them at all. This is the shortest path to a working feature and it is fully switched off.
findings.evidence: ProjectTokenService.cs:340-394; ProjectTokensController.cs:70-110 (501s; git diff HEAD shows allocate/* stubbed in-flight, distribute already 501 at HEAD); AuthorizationPolicies.AdminApiKey on every allocation route; app/portfolio/page.tsx:76-84
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: the thesis-native payout exists in code and no user can trigger it.
findings.recommended: Re-enable allocate/pbi + distribute behind project-owner authorization and an atomic RESERVED→DISTRIBUTED transition keyed by the TaskCommerceAgreement id; that is a smaller job than the AZOA settlement path and needs no crypto.

findings.title: Soulbound BRONZE→DIAMOND tiers never reach chain in AZOA mode, revoke is gated, and there are two unrelated tier systems
findings.detail: CredentialUtilityService.GrantAndMintAsync calls IAlgorandService.MintSoulboundASAAsync(_platformAddress, …). Under Algorand:Provider=Azoa that adapter returns a Failure by design ('address→avatar mapping is unavailable here') and the credential is kept as 'valid off-chain'; ClawbackASAAsync and BurnASAAsync are 'deferred'. UpgradeTierAsync is DB-only and up-only. Default config is Provider=Simulated. AZOA's side: CredentialRevoke is in NotEnabledActionNodeTypes, and the recipient opt-in every ASA transfer needs (CredentialController.cs:58 says so itself) has no caller anywhere in AZOA — OptInAsync exists only on the interface. Separately, User.tier is recomputed from XP thresholds on every XP event, independent of MembershipCredential.tier. Net: 'portable credential' today is two DB columns that can disagree.
findings.evidence: CredentialUtilityService.cs:97-103,163-195; AzoaBackedAlgorandService.cs:188-207,291-312; appsettings.json:10; NotEnabledActionNodeTypes.cs:34-40; IBlockchainProviderModule.cs:39 (only OptInAsync reference); XPEventService.cs:72,202-210; CredentialController.cs:58
findings.thesis_impact: Users see a tier badge; nothing behind it is portable or revocable. Not a crypto-concept leak — it is a promise with no substance.
findings.recommended: Route credential issuance through AZOA's new POST /api/credential/issue/{recipientUserId} via a dapp:manager tenant credential, and make XP tier derive from (or be replaced by) the credential tier.

findings.title: Docs claim the credential rail is inert with no third-party issuance — but the issue route landed in fa2dfcf and nothing was updated
findings.detail: AZOA README, API_SYNC and tracks.md all state 'the only mint path stamps issuer = holder'. CredentialController now has a role-gated POST issue/{recipientUserId} that stamps issuer = caller and recipient = route id (D41 Phase 0). The track metadata is still 'pending', the SDK has no issueCredential, CredentialRevoke is still blocked, and ArdaNova's CredentialUtilityService does not know the route exists. Stale status in both directions: docs say less than code does, and code is less usable than the route suggests.
findings.evidence: CredentialController.cs:75-113; git log -S 'issue/{recipientUserId' → fa2dfcf 2026-09-07; README.md:122; API_SYNC.md:234-239; conductor/tracks.md:54; conductor/tracks/credential-third-party-issuance_20260906/metadata.json:3 (status pending); grep issueCredential in sdk → none
findings.thesis_impact: Indirect — a session reading the docs will re-design what already exists.
findings.recommended: Update README/API_SYNC/tracks.md to 'issuance route landed, revoke still gated', add the SDK method, and mark the track in-flight.

findings.title: Escrow UI is orphaned, the reachable dispute page cannot resolve anything, and the unused release dialog asks users for a 'Transaction reference'
findings.detail: ReleaseDialog, EscrowDetailCard and DisputeForm are imported by no page; only the status badge/timeline/detail are used, on /admin/disputes, which has a single query and no mutation. Backend has DisputeAsync but no ResolveAsync (neither the interface nor the controller). The 20-dispute-escrow-ui spec claims 'Backend Complete: Create, Release, Dispute, Resolve' — Create is 501, Release is 503 in-flight, Resolve does not exist. If ReleaseDialog were ever mounted it would ask a funder to type an opaque 12-200 char transaction reference — a crypto concept surfaced to a non-crypto user, and the same client-asserted-proof pattern the hardening just removed.
findings.evidence: grep 'components/escrow' outside that folder → only app/admin/disputes/page.tsx:17-19; app/admin/disputes/page.tsx:126 (only query); release-dialog.tsx:36,114-120; lib/commerce/escrow-release.ts:5; ITaskEscrowService.cs (no Resolve); conductor/tracks/20-dispute-escrow-ui/spec.md:5-11; documentation/ARCHITECTURE.md:221,1552; README.md:109
findings.thesis_impact: A disputing worker or funder reaches a page with no outcome.
findings.recommended: Delete ReleaseDialog/EscrowDetailCard/DisputeForm or mount them behind the real flow; drop txHash from every client contract; correct the three stale docs.

findings.title: What is a worker's 'stake', concretely?
findings.detail: Three incompatible representations coexist: (a) ProjectTask.equityReward (owner-set decimal, shown as '{n} tokens'), (b) TaskCommerceAgreement.awardAmount in ProjectTokenConfig.unitName at assetScale (from the bid), (c) TokenAllocation.tokenAmount per PBI credited into TokenBalance. None is linked to any on-chain asset. Only the owner can say which one is the record of stake and whether stake must ever be a real ASA.
findings.thesis_impact: Determines whether any crypto concept must ever surface: (c) needs none; a real ASA needs custody, opt-in and a hold.
options: Stake = TokenBalance ledger units of the project token config (off-chain, exchangeable later via the swap rail)
Stake = units of a real per-project ASA held in the worker's AZOA custodial wallet
Stake = equityReward on the task as a bare number with no ledger
findings.recommended: Option 1, and collapse equityReward/awardAmount into one field that creates the TokenAllocation reservation at bid-accept.

findings.title: Who funds the hold — project supply, the owner's personal holdings, or the platform?
findings.detail: TaskEscrow.shareId points at a ProjectShare and funderId at the accepting user, implying the OWNER's personal shares back the bounty; the gated-commerce spec says accept 'reserves its agreed project token award' from project supply; the Task Bounty DAG refunds to 'project treasury'. Three different funding sources, none implemented.
findings.thesis_impact: Decides whether a founder must personally 'give up shares' (a crypto-ish mental model) or the project simply has a contributor pool.
options: Contributor pool: reserve against ProjectTokenConfig.contributorSupply at accept
Owner-funded: debit the owner's TokenBalance/ProjectShare at accept
Platform-funded advance
findings.recommended: Contributor pool — it is what 09-tokenomics already describes and needs no per-owner wallet action.

findings.title: Code has already decided: a worker must pass KYC and hold a wallet BEFORE being assigned any paid task
findings.detail: IAzoaValueEligibilityService.RequireReadyAsync demands identityReady + KYC Approved + walletReady + walletId + walletAddress. It is enforced for both owner and bidder at bid-accept, for the assignee at task create/update whenever equityReward>0, and again at outbox dispatch. So a worker cannot be offered stake-paid work until identity verification completes — a product policy nobody wrote down. The gate UI is mostly clean ('Account setup', 'Identity check', 'Managed payment account') but it renders a shortened wallet address as the payment-account detail, and the verification page's copy talks about 'wallet custody'.
findings.evidence: AzoaValueEligibilityService.cs:46-54; TaskCommerceService.cs:92-105; TasksController.cs:136-144,222-246; EconomicOutboxDispatchService.cs:130-139; custodial-account-card.tsx:87-92 (compactReference(walletAddress)); settings/verification/page.tsx:253
findings.thesis_impact: Every worker hits KYC before their first paid task; a wallet address is the first crypto artefact they see.
options: Gate at settlement only (assign freely, verify before payout)
Gate at accept (current)
Gate at accept for owner, at settlement for worker
findings.recommended: Gate the worker at settlement, not at assignment, and replace the wallet-address detail with a neutral 'Ready' state.

findings.title: Guild bidding carries no guild economics
findings.detail: A bid's guildId is copied onto the task; the agreement's contributorUserId is the individual bidder; there is no guild split, treasury share, or guild payout anywhere in Application services. 'Bring in a guild for a stake' resolves to 'pay one person'.
findings.evidence: TaskCommerceService.cs:136,157; grep guildShare|guild.*payout|split in Services/Implementations → none
findings.thesis_impact: Guild members other than the bidder get nothing; surfaces later as a fairness complaint, not a crypto one.
findings.recommended: Either drop guildId from commerce or add a guild-level TokenAllocation with a declared split at bid time.

findings.title: An unverified worker's settlement would retry silently forever
findings.detail: When the gateway is eventually enabled, DispatchIfEligibleAsync returns Retry('AZOA_ACCOUNT_NOT_READY') for a recipient who has not passed KYC; the outbox backs off to 300s and keeps going with no notification or user-facing state. Combined with the accept-time gate this is mostly unreachable today, but a KYC that expires/rejects after acceptance lands here.
findings.thesis_impact: Worker sees 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' indefinitely with no reason.
findings.recommended: Surface AZOA_ACCOUNT_NOT_READY on the commerce page with the 'Complete setup' link.

verticals.thesis_verdict: No. A worker cannot be paid in stake today by any route, on HEAD or with the in-flight hardening applied: bid-accept creates an agreement that never advances past ACCEPTED, task completion stamps a timestamp, the escrow endpoints answer 501/503, the AZOA allocation path has no caller and would mint an unrelated asset if it did, the off-chain project-token distribute path is 501, and the Task Bounty action DAG is published by nobody. D14 remains true — nothing anywhere can hold. The encouraging part: when a payout does happen, the worker will not need to know what an ASA is — every reachable surface speaks in 'project-token award', 'allocation' and 'managed payment account'. The crypto leak is at the front door, not the payout: code has silently decided that both owner and worker must finish KYC and be provisioned a custodial wallet (whose address the account card displays) before a stake-paid task can even be accepted. Fix order that respects the thesis: reserve stake in the DB at accept, re-enable the off-chain TokenBalance distribute behind owner auth, move the worker's KYC gate to settlement, and only then decide whether stake ever becomes a real ASA.

verticals.feature: Internal token economy: ARDA token, per-project equity ASAs, project-token→ARDA→USD payouts, treasury-backed deterministic rates, fungible mint, Tinyman swap, D16 USD-at-time stamping
