findings.title: The loop never closes: no token-to-dollars path exists in any layer
findings.detail: Payout request AND payout processing both return 503 at the controller (PayoutsController.cs:28-38) and the service layer refuses processing outright (PayoutService.cs:143-146: 'Payout processing is disabled until a verified provider transfer and durable settlement reconciliation are available'). The withdraw page is cancel-only ('Payouts paused', withdraw/page.tsx:161-166) and settings/payouts says 'Payouts are safely disabled' (:27-30). Underneath, there is no fiat rail anywhere: AZOA's IValueRailProvider is only ever extended by IBlockchainProvider (Interfaces/IBlockchainProvider.cs:17, no fiat implementation), fiat-sidecar exposes only checkout.ts + webhook.ts (fiat-sidecar/src/routes/, no transfer/Connect route), and the spec's USDCa stablecoin leg (09-tokenomics/spec.md:9,:61) has ZERO occurrences in ArdaNova code (grep 'USDCa|USDC' over api-server/src returns nothing). Work -> token -> dollars is therefore unreachable today at every layer, not merely gated.
findings.thesis_impact: A worker who finished a task cannot get paid, and the UI tells them so in three places. This is the thesis defect regardless of vocabulary.
options: Stripe Connect transfer route in fiat-sidecar + AZOA fiat IValueRailProvider (D9) with the D10 reversal-event pipeline
USDCa on Algorand via AZOA Transfer allocation (forces users to hold a stablecoin — a crypto concept)
Keep payouts off-platform (manual/ACH) and record only the ledger fact in AZOA
findings.recommended: Stripe Connect via fiat-sidecar + D9 fiat rail; USDCa violates the thesis by design

findings.title: ARDA token cannot exist: nothing ever mints it or sets circulating supply, so every rate/conversion/swap/payout preview fails
findings.detail: No production code writes isPlatformToken=true (only '= false' at TokenBalanceService.cs:119; grep over api-server/src finds no other writer), so GetArdaBalanceAsync always fails 'ARDA balance not found' (:54-67) and GetPortfolioAsync hard-codes ArdaBalance=null and 0 USD totals (:71-86). PlatformTreasury.ardaCirculatingSupply is only ever assigned 0 (TreasuryService.cs:257) and no seeder outside tests touches it (repo-wide grep: only ExchangeService/SwapService/TreasuryService/entity/tests/schema files). Consequently ExchangeService.GetArdaValueAsync always fails 'circulating supply is zero' (:55-59), CalculateConversionAsync fails (:83-88), SwapService.GetSwapPreviewAsync fails (:84-85), and PayoutService.RequestPayoutAsync would unlock and fail at step 4 (:94-110). The invest page's 'Informational ARDA equivalent' / 'Reference value per ARDA' rows (invest/page.tsx:499-505) can never render a number.
findings.thesis_impact: Every 'what is this worth in dollars' surface a sponsor or worker sees is dead. The intermediary token the whole economy is routed through has no genesis.
options: Mint ARDA as a single fungible ASA via AZOA /api/nft/fungible-mint at platform bootstrap and back it 1:1 from treasury inflow (spec §Deterministic rates)
Drop ARDA as a user-visible intermediary; keep it as an internal accounting unit and quote users only in USD
Remove ARDA entirely; project-token -> USD directly off treasury book value
findings.recommended: Option 2: keep ARDA internal (or remove), never show 'ARDA' to a sponsor — the invest page already exposes it

findings.title: Sponsorship checkout is unreachable by construction, not by config
findings.detail: FundingIntentService.CreateCheckoutAsync returns Conflict unless _settlementReadiness.IsReady (:69-70). IsReady requires the settlement gateway to implement ISelectedNodeSettlementCapability with CanDispatch/CanReconcile/HasCurrentOperatorAttestation (AzoaFundingSettlementReadiness.cs:26-38), but the ONLY IAzoaSettlementGateway implementation is DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway (DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway.cs:6) — no config flag can make it ready. Independently, checkout also requires config.assetId to be non-empty (FundingIntentService.cs:85-86 'requires a verified asset id before funding checkout'), and nothing in the backend ever assigns ProjectTokenConfig.assetId (grep 'assetId =' hits only credentials/allocation DTO defaults). EnableFundingCheckout also defaults false (AzoaSettings.cs:56). The invest page honestly shows 'checkout remains unavailable' (:282-284).
findings.thesis_impact: A sponsor cannot sponsor. The first thesis action (fund a project) is blocked before Stripe is even reached.
options: Implement a real IAzoaSettlementGateway (AzoaNodeClient-backed) with operator attestation and enable the outbox worker
Populate ProjectTokenConfig.assetId by minting the project ASA at CreateConfigAsync via AzoaBackedAlgorandService.CreateFungibleASAAsync
Temporarily allow checkout without assetId (DB-ledger-only project units) so sponsorship works before chain
findings.recommended: Both 1 and 2 are required for the designed path; 3 is the thesis-first shortcut if chain is truly implementation detail

findings.title: A completed Stripe payment credits nothing: the legacy allocation path has no callers and the new path is inert
findings.detail: StripeWebhookController.DispatchAsync routes payment_intent.succeeded exclusively to FundingIntentService.RecordPaymentSucceededAsync (StripeWebhookController.cs:107-117), which writes an EconomicSettlement PENDING_DISPATCH + EconomicOutbox PENDING (FundingIntentService.cs:408-435) and explicitly does not allocate tokens, credit treasury, or evaluate Gate 1. The legacy StripeService.HandlePaymentSucceededAsync — the only code that calls AllocateToInvestorAsync + ProcessFundingInflowAsync + EvaluateGate1Async (StripeService.cs:211-248) — has zero callers outside its own interface (grep over API/Application). The outbox worker that would drain PENDING rows is unregistered unless Azoa:EnableSettlementOutboxWorker=true (DependencyInjection.cs:146-147; default false at AzoaSettings.cs:65), and even then the gateway is Disabled. gated-commerce plan.md:138-141 admits 'this creates no HTTP call, AZOA effect, allocation, payout, or settlement completion'.
findings.thesis_impact: Even if checkout were opened, the sponsor's money would land in Stripe and produce no equity, no treasury backing, no Gate 1. The chain of custody from dollars to ownership is cut at the first link.
options: Wire the outbox dispatcher to a real gateway that calls AZOA POST /api/allocation/{userId} and then credit local balances on confirmation
Re-attach the legacy HandlePaymentSucceededAsync inside the same transaction as RecordPaymentSucceededAsync so local ledger effects happen now and AZOA effects later
findings.recommended: Option 1, but stage it: local credit on signed provider success (thesis-visible), AZOA mirror asynchronously

findings.title: Per-project equity ASAs are DB rows; AZOA fungible-mint is never called by ArdaNova
findings.detail: ProjectTokenService.cs (630 lines) contains no reference to IAlgorandService, Azoa, Mint, or assetId — CreateConfigAsync (:64-110) writes a ProjectTokenConfig row with assetId null; DistributeAsync (:340-395) credits a TokenBalance row. IAlgorandService is injected only by CredentialUtilityService (grep 'IAlgorandService _' across Application/API). AzoaBackedAlgorandService.CreateFungibleASAAsync (the 'CLEAN MAP' to POST /api/nft/fungible-mint, :135-186) has no callers besides the three IAlgorandService implementations. AZOA's endpoint, manager, SDK method and operator page are all real (NftController.cs:101, FungibleTokenManager.cs:57, client.ts:1437, fungible-mint/page.tsx:99) — but ArdaNova never dials them. The 'audit trail on Algorand' promised at spec.md:14-16 does not exist for project tokens.
findings.thesis_impact: Neutral for the non-crypto user today (they never see the chain), but it means 'real ownership' and 'portable credentials' from the thesis are marketing: equity is a Postgres integer.
options: Mint the project ASA once at CreateConfigAsync with total=totalSupply, decimals=assetScale and store assetId
Accept DB-only equity for launch and mint retroactively on Gate 2
findings.recommended: Option 1 — it also unblocks the assetId gate in finding 3

findings.title: ArdaNova's fungible-mint wire model does not match AZOA's DTO; if ever wired it fails on 'zero total'
findings.detail: ArdaNova sends {chainType, name, unitName, totalSupply: string} (AzoaFungibleMintRequest, AzoaBackedAlgorandService.cs:347-355). AZOA binds FungibleMintRequest {ChainType, Name, UnitName, Total: ulong, Decimals: int, HolonId?} (FungibleMintRequest.cs:29-56). System.Text.Json ignores the unknown 'totalSupply', Total stays 0, and FungibleTokenManager.ValidateSupply rejects a zero total before broadcast (:256-273). Decimals is never sent, so even a fixed field name would mint a 0-decimal asset regardless of ProjectTokenConfig.assetScale (0..18). On the response side ArdaNova expects txHash/operationId (:358-366) which FungibleTokenResult does not carry (FungibleTokenResult.cs:15-33) — non-fatal (nullable) but the TxHash fallback logic is dead. tracks.md lists the provider adapter as '[~]' shipped-behind-flag; the clean-map path has never been exercised against AZOA.
findings.thesis_impact: Hidden until someone flips Algorand:Provider=Azoa and calls CreateFungibleASAAsync; then every project-token mint fails with a message about 'zero total' that no user can act on.
options: Rename to total + add decimals=assetScale in AzoaFungibleMintRequest
Add a contract test in ArdaNova that round-trips the DTO against AZOA's OpenAPI
findings.recommended: Both; the integration contract (§11.3) pins no DTO, which is how this drifted

findings.title: A task reward mints a brand-new 0-decimal ASA per reward instead of moving project-token units
findings.detail: AzoaAllocationService.AllocateRewardAsync builds Kind=Mint with Name=assetName (:62-67) — the plan says kind=Transfer (treasury-reward plan.md:41-42), a code/plan contradiction. In AZOA, AllocationKind.Mint creates an NftMintRequest + a 'Mint' BlockchainOperation with Amount=NetAmount (AllocationManager.cs:250-292); ExecuteMintAsync calls provider.MintAsync (BlockchainOperationManager.cs:444-464) which is CreateAsaCoreAsync(total=amount, decimals=0, manager/reserve/freeze/clawback = the recipient's custodial wallet) (AlgorandProvider.cs:490-510). So each reward is a fresh asset, fungible with nothing, named after the project, and a user with 12 tasks holds 12 unrelated ASAs. The alternative, Kind=Transfer, is denied whenever the node fee schedule has TransferBps>0 ('Transfer node fees require on-chain treasury settlement, which is not configured', AllocationManager.cs:444-448). Whoever first wires the reward trigger is choosing the on-chain representation of equity.
findings.thesis_impact: Invisible today (no caller). If wired as-is, the user's 'equity' becomes a pile of one-off assets that can never be summed, swapped, or paid out as one balance — the opposite of transparent ownership.
options: Mint the project ASA once; rewards = Kind=Transfer from a project reserve wallet, with TransferBps=0 or treasury settlement configured
Keep Mint-per-reward and treat the ASAs as non-fungible receipts (then stop calling them equity)
Keep rewards off-chain (DB balance) and only settle on chain at payout
findings.recommended: Option 1; fix the plan/code mismatch first

findings.title: D16 USD-at-time stamping is inert and, if ever wired, would price ASA transfers as native ALGO
findings.detail: IValueRateSource has no DI registration anywhere (grep over Program.cs/Extensions/Services is empty); BlockchainOperationManager falls back to UnpricedValueRateSource.Instance (:42), so every operation_log row has the five value_* columns NONE (OperationLog.cs:20). The analytics surface reports this honestly via UnpricedEntryCount (AnalyticsResponses.cs:159,226-240). The latent trap: TryReadRailAmount parses Burn/Transfer amounts with ValueDimension.NativeChainAsset unconditionally (BlockchainOperationManager.cs:661-666) even when the op carries a SourceTokenId (an ASA, :501). The first real rate source will stamp a transfer of N project-token units as N microAlgos. Swap/Exchange ops are never stamped at all (:642-655), so the one operation that IS a price discovery event leaves no USD record.
findings.thesis_impact: No user-visible effect today; it breaks the 'transparent settlement' promise and any tax/statement export the moment real value moves.
options: Register a rate source that returns null for ChainAsset dimensions it cannot price and fix TryReadRailAmount to use ValueDimension.ChainAsset(SourceTokenId)
Have ArdaNova stamp USD on its own ledger (it already computes the rate) and never rely on AZOA's stamp
findings.recommended: Both: ArdaNova owns the rate (D7/D16), AZOA should record ArdaNova's decided USD figure as the stamp rather than quoting its own

findings.title: Rate authority is correctly ArdaNova-side, but the money math is double/int with silent truncation
findings.detail: Consistent with D7/D16, AZOA computes no economics (FungibleMintRequest.cs:15-17 'AZOA derives no economic meaning'; AllocationRequest.cs:22-25). ArdaNova owns the rate: token value = fundingRaised/totalSupply (ExchangeService.cs:40), ARDA value = (index+liquid+ops)/circulating (:60-62). But all of it is double: usdValue = tokenAmount * projectTokenValue, ardaAmount = usdValue/ardaValue, then (long)ardaAmount (:98-105), (int)preview.ArdaAmount (PayoutService.cs:126), int tokenAmount (:69), (int)((usdAmount/valuationBase)*totalSupply) in the legacy funding path (StripeService.cs:198), treasury inflow split in double (TreasuryService.cs:31,43-45). financial-engine-domain-hardening plan.md:37 lists '[ ] Replace funding/project-token double values on value paths' as unstarted. SwapService uses decimal (:91) — two numeric models for the same rate.
findings.thesis_impact: A worker converting a small balance can be truncated to 0 ARDA and told nothing; a sponsor's displayed 'reference value' can drift from what settles.
findings.recommended: Finish the FixedScaleAmount migration before any of the rate endpoints are user-visible

findings.title: Algorand swap is not executable by anyone but an algosdk developer; SDK Tinyman defaults decimals to 6 on the execute path
findings.detail: Backend TinymanDexAdapter.GetQuoteAsync computes a real constant-product quote in base units (:39-155), but BuildSwapTransactionAsync returns no transaction — only a Message telling the caller to build 'app_opt_in, swap, fee payment' with algosdk (:160-178); SwapManager passes that through (:87-121) and SwapNodeHandler does the same inside a durable action (:34-39). The SDK's own Tinyman adapter defaults assetIn/assetOut decimals to 6 when the caller omits them, with a TODO admitting quotes for non-6-decimal ASAs 'will be inaccurate' (tinyman.ts:167-173), and re-uses that default in generateTxns on the execute path (:267-276) — project tokens with assetScale 0..18 (ProjectTokenService.cs:78) would be mis-sized. ArdaNova's own SwapService.ExecuteSwapAsync is a hard stub (:117-127). The 'deterministic, treasury-backed, no AMM' spec (spec.md:17,155) never intended Tinyman for project tokens; the AMM path exists only for the AZOA operator page.
findings.thesis_impact: The 'Exchange' feature a user sees (swap-preview.tsx token -> ARDA -> token) has no execution path; the only executable swap requires the user to construct Algorand transaction groups.
options: Resolve decimals from indexer in the SDK adapter (remove the ?? 6)
Implement server-side Tinyman tx-group build + custodial sign in AZOA
Keep project-token exchange strictly treasury-rate (no AMM) and drop Tinyman from the ArdaNova path
findings.recommended: Option 3 for ArdaNova; option 1 regardless because the SDK ships publicly

findings.title: SDK Algorand amount handling is inconsistent and float-based
findings.detail: buildPaymentTx converts ALGO with Math.round(Number(amount) * 1_000_000) (provider.ts:470) while buildAsaTransferTx uses Number(params.amount) as raw base units (:493) — the same TransferParams.amount means 'decimal ALGO' for one branch and 'base units' for the other, and both lose precision above 2^53 despite the SDK's 'all amounts are strings for arbitrary precision' rule. supportsBridging is hard-coded true on both providers (algorand/provider.ts:104, solana/provider.ts:52) while backend bridge primitives are fail-closed/disabled (RUNBOOK D26; memory bridge-unsafe).
findings.thesis_impact: Low today (ArdaNova's browser SDK layer is read-only, lib/azoa-sdk/client.ts:13-20); bites any consumer that signs client-side.
findings.recommended: Make ASA/ALGO amounts both base-unit strings parsed with BigInt; derive supportsBridging from a capability probe

findings.title: Where the UI works, it teaches tokenomics: ARDA, project units, rates per ARDA, Algorand addresses
findings.detail: invest/page.tsx shows 'Informational ARDA equivalent', 'Reference value per ARDA', and a disclaimer that 'A project-unit supply percentage is not equity, governance power, a redemption right, or a guaranteed USD value' (:499-525) — a sponsor must parse three asset concepts to give money. swap-preview.tsx renders 'via ARDA', '$x/ARDA', 'TOKEN -> ARDA -> TOKEN | Rate:' (:76-122); conversion-chain.tsx '1 TICKER = N ARDA' (:67). settings/wallets asks for 'Your Algorand public address' and explains private keys/mnemonics are never requested (:146-160,279). The custodial-account card is well-phrased ('account setup', components/azoa/AGENTS.md:29-35) but still surfaces 'wallet' as a readiness step with a shortened address (:86-91). By contrast the thesis says wallets, addresses and rates are implementation detail.
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: the sponsorship screen requires the user to understand a two-hop token conversion to interpret the number they are paying.
findings.recommended: Quote sponsors and workers in USD and ownership-% only; move ARDA/rates to an 'advanced/statement' view; treat external Algorand wallets as an opt-in power-user page

findings.title: Which asset is 'the project token' on chain, and who holds its reserve?
findings.detail: Three incompatible representations are on disk: (a) ProjectTokenConfig as a DB integer with optional assetId (never set); (b) AZOA fungible-mint creating one ASA per project with tenant-supplied total/decimals whose manager/reserve/freeze/clawback are the caller's custodial wallet (FungibleTokenManager.cs:147-157); (c) AllocationKind.Mint creating one ASA per reward. Only the owner can decide whether a project has a reserve wallet (which user/tenant custodies it), whether decimals = assetScale, and whether clawback stays enabled for equity (it must for D19 credential revocation, but revocable equity is a governance statement).
findings.thesis_impact: Determines whether a worker's holdings ever appear as one balance.
options: One ASA per project minted at config time into a project reserve wallet; rewards/investments are transfers
DB-only equity; chain used only for payouts/credentials
ASA per reward (status quo code path)
findings.recommended: Option 1

findings.title: Is ARDA a user-facing currency or an internal accounting unit?
findings.detail: The spec makes ARDA the universal exchange medium with a treasury-backed deterministic rate (spec.md:149-155) and the UI exposes it; but there is no mint, no circulating supply, and no reason a social-democrat sponsor needs to see it. If it stays internal, ExchangeService can collapse to project-token -> USD directly and the ARDA balance/portfolio endpoints (TokenBalanceController.cs:37-44) can go. If it stays user-facing, its genesis, backing ratio, and whether it is itself an ASA (spec.md:8 says yes) must be decided before anything else in this feature can compute a number.
findings.thesis_impact: Directly controls how much tokenomics a sponsor must read.
options: Internal only, USD-quoted UI
User-facing platform token with published backing
Remove
findings.recommended: Internal only

findings.title: The 'Simulated' provider defaults make every local demo look like the economy works
findings.detail: appsettings.json sets Algorand:Provider=Simulated and Azoa:Mode=Simulated (ArdaNova.API/appsettings.json:10,18); SimulatedAlgorandService fabricates asset ids (SimulatedAlgorandService.cs:22,98). Combined with the DB-only ledger, a developer can walk create-config -> allocate -> distribute -> balance and see numbers, while none of finding 1-5 is exercised. The gated-commerce plan is explicit that nothing is 'economically activated merely because these generated models exist' (plan.md:150-155), but the defaults decide otherwise for anyone who does not read it.
findings.thesis_impact: Indirect: QA against the simulated stack cannot surface the thesis failures above.
findings.recommended: Add a startup banner/health field that says 'economy: simulated / disabled' and keep QA checklists pointed at it

layers_absent: Fiat payout rail: no IValueRailProvider fiat implementation in AZOA; fiat-sidecar has checkout + webhook only (no Connect transfer)
ARDA genesis: no mint, no ardaCirculatingSupply writer, no isPlatformToken=true balance writer
Project-token on-chain mint call site: ProjectTokenService never calls IAlgorandService/AzoaBackedAlgorandService; ProjectTokenConfig.assetId never written

ArdaNova payout processing (503 at controller, refusal at service) and ArdaNova swap execution (stub failure)
USDCa stablecoin leg promised by spec: zero code
Server-side Algorand swap execution: Tinyman adapter returns a build-it-yourself message; SwapNodeHandler inherits it
verticals.thesis_verdict: No. A non-crypto user cannot complete any leg of the loop today. Sponsor: checkout is blocked by construction (readiness needs a gateway capability that no implementation has, plus an assetId that nothing writes). Worker: rewards never dispatch (no caller), and even a DB-credited balance cannot become dollars (payout request and processing both 503; ARDA has no genesis so every conversion preview fails; no fiat rail exists in AZOA or the sidecar; USDCa is spec-only). Exchange: ArdaNova's ExecuteSwap is a stub and AZOA's Algorand swap hands back instructions to build an algosdk transaction group. The one thing that works — the AZOA operator harness minting a fungible ASA — is never invoked by ArdaNova, and ArdaNova's adapter for it sends the wrong field names. The plumbing that does exist is careful (fail-closed gates, idempotency keys, honest 'unpriced' analytics, ArdaNova owning the rate per D7/D16), but it is unwired, and where the ArdaNova UI does function it teaches ARDA, project units, per-ARDA rates and Algorand addresses to the very audience the thesis says must never need them.

findings.title: Two governance systems exist and never meet; nobody has decided which is the vote of record
findings.detail: AZOA ships a tenant-electorate, KYC-uniqueness, claim-ledger governance primitive (D20/D39/D40) as three action nodes. ArdaNova ships its own complete EF governance: Proposal/Vote tables, project-scoped routes on ProjectsController, quorum/threshold, comments, DelegatedVote share-weighted delegation, and a full Next.js UI. The ArdaNova backend contains no reference to any AZOA governance node type and the azoa-sdk exposes none. Whoever wires the first adapter decides implicitly whether the AZOA claim ledger or the ArdaNova Vote table is authoritative, whether votes are one-human (AZOA D3) or one-member (ArdaNova), and whether they are mutable until close (AZOA D40) or immutable ('User has already voted', GovernanceServices.cs:200-203). ArdaNova product.md:13 additionally promises 'on-chain decision making', which neither implementation does (AZOA D42 is off-chain Tier-1; ArdaNova Vote.txHash is never written).
findings.evidence: oasis-sleek: Services/Actions/Handlers/GovernanceVoteNodeHandler.cs:63-187; Services/Governance/GovernanceClaimLedgerTally.cs:63-88. ardanova: api-server/src/ArdaNova.API/Controllers/ProjectsController.cs:766-935; ArdaNova.Application/Services/Implementations/GovernanceServices.cs:188-225,263-309; ArdaNova.Domain/Models/Entities/DelegatedVote.cs:28-32; conductor/product.md:13; grep GovernanceVote|GovernanceProposal|GovernanceTally in api-server/src → 0 hits
options: A) AZOA is the vote of record: ArdaNova's Proposal/Vote become a display cache fed by AZOA proposal/claim-ledger results; ArdaNova electorate (project members) must be expressed to AZOA (today impossible — see electorate finding)
B) ArdaNova is the vote of record: AZOA governance nodes stay gated/unused for ArdaNova; AZOA only anchors tally hashes later (D42) — simplest for the thesis, wastes the D39 work
C) Hybrid: ArdaNova counts, AZOA's IPersonUniquenessGate is called per ballot for one-human-one-vote only
findings.recommended: B or C. AZOA's node-shaped voting cannot serve a social-platform vote button without a new REST/SDK surface anyway; decide franchise (stake vs membership vs human) first, then pick the substrate.
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: a sponsor or worker cannot vote today on either system end to end; and the two implementations encode different answers to 'who gets a vote'.

findings.title: In AZOA, casting a vote means executing a workflow whose option is baked into node config — there is no 'vote' API
findings.detail: GovernanceVoteNodeConfig has exactly two fields, ProposalHolonId and Option; the option is static node config, and the voter is the run's runner (ActionNodeStepHandler: acting user = run.UserId). So for members to choose yes vs no, a consumer must publish separate actions per option (or bind Option through a run./upstream node output) and have every voter execute the correct action via POST /api/action/{id}/execute. There is no POST vote, no GET my-vote, no GET results; the tally is only the JSON output of a GovernanceTally node execution. The SDK has no governance methods. Even after the gate lifts, ArdaNova cannot put a vote button on this without building that surface.
findings.evidence: Services/Actions/Handlers/GovernanceVoteNodeHandler.cs:298-305 (config), :90-94 (config deserialised from context.Node.Config); Services/Actions/Workflow/ActionNodeStepHandler.cs:149-158; Controllers/ActionController.cs:145-163; Services/Actions/Handlers/GovernanceTallyNodeHandler.cs:146-156; sdk/azoa-wallet/src/api/client.ts:702-705 (type union only); ls Controllers/ shows no consumer governance controller
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — 'execute this action run' is a workflow-engine concept, not a social-platform concept; the option cannot be chosen at vote time through any first-class API.

findings.title: AZOA's electorate is 'the acting tenant' or the whole node — never a project's sponsors and workers
findings.detail: electorateTenant is pinned from context.ActingTenantId at proposal creation; IsInElectorate compares only that. ActingTenantId comes solely from an act_as_tenant claim stamped on tenant-driven child credentials; a plain user JWT yields null, so a proposal created by an ordinary user records electorate 'node' and every verified user on the node may vote. There is no project/holon/membership-scoped franchise at all. The thesis needs 'sponsors and workers of THIS project'; AZOA cannot express it.
options: Express electorate as a holon (project) membership predicate evaluated at vote time
Have ArdaNova act via tenant-driven child credentials so electorate = ArdaNova tenant, and let ArdaNova pre-filter project members before executing the vote action (trust ArdaNova as the gate)
Keep AZOA governance tenant-wide (co-op-wide referenda) and leave project decisions to ArdaNova
findings.recommended: Second or third; a holon-membership electorate is a new design, not a gate-lift item.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — project-level decisions are the product; tenant-wide is the wrong unit.

findings.title: The counting QUESTION is still owner-rewritable through HolonManager.UpdateAsync — the actual reason the gate must stay
findings.detail: UpdateAsync checks only ownership and then blind-merges metadata. The proposal's owner (the user who ran GovernanceProposalCreate) can PUT /api/holon/{id} and rewrite options, status, opensAt, closesAt, uniquenessScope and electorateTenant after ballots are cast. Concrete effects: (1) rewriting uniquenessScope Tenant→Global or electorateTenant changes the scope value the tally counts in (TryResolveUniquenessScopeValue), so every claim already recorded under the old scope silently disappears from the count while the tallyHash still looks valid; (2) rewriting status to Closed shuts voting early; (3) closesAt cannot thaw an existing claim (decision_closes_at is pinned on the row) but CAN extend the window for voters with no row yet; (4) options can be replaced — I did not verify whether CountVotesOfRecordAsync drops or keeps decisions for de-listed options. Only uniquenessOperationKey is protected (derived-key equality). No test covers proposal rewrites; the AC4 test rewrites only the ballot receipt.
findings.evidence: Managers/HolonManager.cs:140-166 (ownership-only + metadata merge); Services/Governance/ConsumerGovernanceHolonTypes.cs:129-158; Services/Actions/Handlers/GovernanceTallyNodeHandler.cs:114-131; GovernanceVoteNodeHandler.cs:149-152 (only the key is checked); Persistence/SurrealDb/Generated/Schemas/person_operation_claim.surql:34-36; tests/AZOA.WebAPI.Tests/Governance/GovernanceVoteOfRecordTests.cs:168 (RewriteBallotOptionsAsync — receipt, not proposal); Services/Governance/AGENTS.md:222-224 acknowledges UpdateAsync still blind-merges
findings.recommended: Freeze GovernanceProposal metadata after the first claim (or after publish) inside HolonManager keyed on AssetType, or snapshot the question (options/scope/electorate/closesAt) onto the claim rows the way decision_closes_at already is, and add the proposal-rewrite attack tests before lifting the gate.
findings.thesis_impact: Indirect — a proposal author can move the outcome after members voted; that is the trust failure the social-democrat audience will notice.

findings.title: ArdaNova's live vote button is dead for everyone except admins: the ACTIVE membership credential it requires cannot be granted anywhere
findings.detail: ProjectsController.CastVote and the tRPC castVote both require an ACTIVE MembershipCredential. Every path that could create one returns 501 / NOT_IMPLEMENTED: MembershipCredentialsController.Grant, CredentialUtilityController.grant-and-mint/check-auto-grant, and the client's membershipCredential.grant router. GrantAsync itself additionally demands KYC PRO. So a project member who clicks vote sees the literal string 'CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED: You need an active membership credential to vote. Credential issuance is a separate authorized workflow.' with no way to obtain one. The UI (proposals-tab) still renders vote controls to members.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the user is told about 'credentials' and 'authorized workflows' and cannot vote.

findings.title: ArdaNova proposals can never resolve: nothing writes PASSED/REJECTED/EXPIRED, 'close' is cancel, and quorum compares a vote count to a percentage
findings.detail: ProposalStatus.PASSED is only ever read (ExecuteProposalAsync requires it) and never assigned anywhere in the source tree, so Execute is unreachable; the client's closeProposal posts to /cancel, yielding CANCELLED. GetVoteSummaryAsync computes quorumReached = totalVotingPower >= proposal.quorum, where the client sends quorum as a percentage (50/66 defaults) and weight is forced to 1 by the controller, so 'quorum 50%' means 50 ballots. The UI still shows 'voting power' and 'quorum %'. None of this is in-flight security work; these are committed defects.
findings.evidence: ardanova: ArdaNova.Application/Services/Implementations/GovernanceServices.cs:287,317 (grep ProposalStatus.PASSED → only :317); ardanova-client/src/lib/api/ardanova/endpoints/projects.ts:695-702; ArdaNova.API/Controllers/ProjectsController.cs:929-931 (Weight = null → 1 at GovernanceServices.cs:211); ardanova-client/src/components/projects/proposals-tab.tsx:353-359,112-122
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — a member who does vote will see a proposal that never passes.

findings.title: What is the franchise for a project decision — verified human, project member, or token/stake weight?
findings.detail: Three incompatible answers are already encoded: AZOA D3 one-verified-human-one-vote via KYC person key (voting requires a bound KYC identity; NoVerifiedIdentity → Ineligible with the single opaque refusal sentence); ArdaNova one-member-one-vote gated by a soulbound credential, weight hard-coded to 1; ArdaNova DelegatedVote delegating 'amount' of a ProjectShare (stake-weighted). Only the owner can say whether a sponsor's voice scales with investment and whether KYC-to-vote is acceptable for the audience.
options: One verified human, one vote (AZOA D3) — needs KYC for every voter
One project member, one vote (ArdaNova today) — needs a credential-issuance path
Stake-weighted (sponsors by investment, workers by earned share) — needs the DelegatedVote/ProjectShare model finished and AZOA's tally extended beyond counts
findings.recommended: Decide before any adapter is written; AZOA's uniqueness gate can serve as an anti-Sybil check under any of the three.
findings.thesis_impact: Direct — 'who gets a say' is the product's social contract.

findings.title: Who may open a proposal, and should AZOA proposals be created by the ArdaNova server on the member's behalf?
findings.detail: In AZOA, a proposal is a node inside an action that must be created (DappDevelop policy) and published, then executed; ordinary end users do not hold DappDevelop, so today only dapp/API-key developers can raise one, and the proposal holon is owned by whoever ran it. In ArdaNova any project member can create (member check in controller and router). If AZOA were the record, ArdaNova would have to author/publish the action and run it under a tenant-driven child credential so electorateTenant is set — none of that exists.
options: ArdaNova server authors and runs the AZOA action on behalf of the member (tenant child credential)
AZOA grows a first-class POST /api/governance/proposals consumer route
Proposals stay ArdaNova-only
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — a member should click 'propose', not 'build and publish a workflow'.

findings.title: Nothing shows a member what they voted or how the vote stands
findings.detail: The AZOA tally is only a node output; there is no results endpoint and no proposal-level running count. The voter's receipt holon is private to the voter and carries option+castAt only; the person_operation_claim ledger is node-operator-only by design and must stay off every consumer read surface. AGENTS.md also records that GET /api/holon/{id} returns any published proposal to every authenticated user on the node (CanRead has no tenant term), so the read surface is simultaneously too wide (cross-tenant proposal text) and too narrow (no counts).
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — a vote you cannot see the result of is not transparent settlement.

findings.title: KYC identity scope vs acting-tenant scope can make a verified ArdaNova user 'NoVerifiedIdentity' at vote time
findings.detail: PersonUniquenessGate resolves the voter's identity binding in KycPersonKeyDeriver.ScopeValue(tenantId) where tenantId is the run's ActingTenantId. Identity bindings are written by KycIdentityBindingService under _deriver.ScopeFor(tenantId) of the KYC call. If ArdaNova users are KYC-bound under the ArdaNova tenant scope (custodial-account/KYC routes are tenant-prefixed) but execute a vote action with a plain user JWT (ActingTenantId=null → node scope), the lookup misses and the vote is refused with the generic ineligible sentence. I did not trace ArdaNova's KYC call to confirm which tenant id it binds under, so this is a plausible trap rather than a confirmed one.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes if it fires — a user who completed verification is told they are not eligible, with no explanation.

findings.title: ArdaNova has governance UI, but none of it touches AZOA, and its MCP exposes only read-only delegation lookups
findings.detail: Answering the brief's question directly: yes, ArdaNova has a governance UI — a /governance feed (read-only; its tRPC mutations throw NOT_IMPLEMENTED) and a live project-tab proposals panel (create/vote/publish/close via api.project.*). All of it targets ArdaNova's own EF tables. The MCP has DelegatedVoteTools (five getters) and no proposal/vote tools; delegation mutations are 501. No component imports azoa-sdk for governance.
findings.thesis_impact: Neutral — the UI shape is right for the thesis; the substrate under it is not connected.

findings.title: What must close before the three governance members leave NotEnabledActionNodeTypes
findings.detail: From the code and Services/Governance/AGENTS.md, the concrete exit list is: (1) close the proposal-metadata rewrite path in HolonManager.UpdateAsync for AssetType GovernanceProposal (or pin the question onto claims) plus attack tests for it — plan.md Phase 3 item 2, not done; (2) decide and record whether node-wide CanRead on published proposals is acceptable (AGENTS.md calls narrowing it 'the follow-up'); (3) resolve the tenant-electorate vs null-tenant behaviour so a proposal raised by a plain user does not enfranchise the whole node; (4) record the Phase 4 adversarial-review verdict ('can a vote that never took a claim still be counted?') — no verdict exists in the tree; (5) flip node-catalog.ts preview rows and the SDK comment, and reduce NotEnabledNodeTypeGateTests.All.HaveCount(4) to 1; (6) update spec/plan/metadata/tracks.md and ArdaNova RUNBOOK §6/contract §6. None of these gives ArdaNova a vote button — that is a separate track the current one does not contain.
options: Lift after items 1-6 (governance usable only by dapp developers via action DAGs)

verticals.thesis_verdict: No. A sponsor or worker cannot vote on a project decision today on either system without meeting a crypto or workflow concept. On AZOA, voting is not an API at all: it is executing an action DAG whose ballot option is fixed in node config, after passing KYC, into an electorate that is 'the tenant' or 'the whole node' rather than the project — and the three nodes are correctly refused at publish and both dispatch seams anyway. The two governance stacks share no code path, encode different franchises (verified human vs member vs share-weighted delegation), and the track docs on both sides still describe a Sybil hole that fa2dfcf already closed. The honest next step is an owner decision on franchise and vote-of-record, then a consumer vote surface — not lifting the gate.

findings.title: No HOLD primitive exists on any layer — escrow, the core sponsor->worker loop, is unbuildable today
findings.detail: AZOA's tenant value door offers exactly two kinds, Mint and Transfer (AllocationRequest.cs:11-18). Nothing in Services/Managers can take value from a sponsor and park it pending an outcome. ArdaNova's TaskEscrow mirrors the hole: CreateAsync writes status NONE (:73); DisputeAsync requires FUNDED (:107) but no code path anywhere sets EscrowStatus.FUNDED (repo-wide grep hits only NONE and DISPUTED), so dispute is unreachable; ReleaseAsync and RefundAsync return hard failures (:83-89, :128-134). ArdaNova's 'refund' is an AZOA Transfer of an NFT-by-Guid record back to the funder (AzoaAllocationService.cs:117-122) — it moves a record, it does not release held fungible value. The runbook already names this (D14 :365-368, D27 :432-433, §7 D :1205-1208) and says a hold needs either an unimplemented TEAL contract or a platform-custodial holding account that custody-Disabled cannot run. Status is honest; the gap is structural, not a bug.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — every non-crypto user. A sponsor cannot escrow a bounty and a worker cannot be paid on completion; the platform's entire economic promise is fail-closed.
findings.recommended: Build HOLD as a Tier-2 node trio (Hold / Release / Refund) on a platform-custodial holding wallet behind KeyCustodyService, with a hold ledger row (holdId, funder, beneficiary, asset, amount, state) as the idempotency anchor; TEAL escrow later. Ship it BEFORE any KMS decision so the fiat design session (F) has a real primitive to specify against.
options: Platform-custodial holding account (fastest; custody exposure = the float)
TEAL escrow contract on Algorand (no custodial float; deploy/call path unimplemented)

findings.title: D36's 'sign-without-export' KMS seam does not exist in code — the derivation interface exports raw key bytes by contract
findings.detail: RUNBOOK D36 (:637-647) says D27's adapter 'is built against an abstract sign-without-export interface behind IPlatformKeyDerivation'. The code contradicts this: IPlatformKeyDerivation has one operation, `bool TryDerive(string configuredSecret, out byte[] key)` (IPlatformKeyDerivation.cs:100) — it takes a config secret and returns raw key bytes to the caller, which is export by definition. PlatformKeyDerivationRegistry.Default holds exactly three config-derivations (Algorand/Solana/Ethereum, :18-23) and ResolvePlatformKeyAsync reads the secret with `_config.GetValue<string>(derivation.PlatformKeyConfigPath)` (KeyCustodyService.cs:257) then passes the bytes to `sign(key)` (:294). Per-user wallets are AES-GCM under `SHA256(AZOA:WalletEncryptionKey)` — a raw hash of a config string, no KDF, no salt (WalletKeyService.cs:27-32). The Production boot guard only rejects empty/placeholder (Program.cs:142-147); the 32-char floor exists only on the DevelopmentOnly tenant path (TenantCustodialAccountManager.cs:93-94). `CustodyMode=KmsHsm` is a string compare that returns 'unavailable' (:507-508). A KMS adapter therefore cannot 'plug in' without changing the interface shape: an HSM never hands out `byte[] key`, it accepts a payload and returns a signature. The whole signer stack (ITransactionSigner takes key bytes) is built around export.
findings.thesis_impact: Indirect but total: D27 blocks all Phase 3 fiat on this, so no real money reaches a user until it lands.
findings.recommended: Replace `TryDerive(secret, out byte[])` with `ISigningKeyHandle { Task<byte[]> SignAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> payload) ; string PublicKey }` resolved per chain; keep the env-backed implementation as one provider that derives in-process, so an HSM/KMS provider implements the same handle without ever surfacing bytes. Update D36's wording to say the seam is NOT yet sign-without-export.
options: Refactor to a sign-only handle now (pre-launch, no compat needed — greenfield rule)
Keep byte-export seam and accept env-backed custody as the terminal design (owner rejected this in D27)

findings.title: CustodyMode=Disabled does not disable custody — the allocation door materialises config-KEK wallets regardless
findings.detail: `CustodialAccounts:CustodyMode` is read in exactly one place: TenantCustodialAccountManager.BuildCapabilities (:79-94), which only decides whether the tenant onboarding route reports walletReady. AllocationManager.EnsureWalletAsync (:215-236) calls `_walletManager.GenerateWalletAsync` whenever the target user has no wallet on the chain — no CustodyMode check, no environment check. Its only gate before that is the KYC value-access gate (:114). So in Production with CustodyMode=Disabled, a tenant POST /api/allocation/{userId} (AllocationController.cs:45, [Authorize]) will mint a platform-custodial wallet encrypted under the config KEK and broadcast into it. docs/TENANT-CUSTODIAL-ONBOARDING.md:66-68 claims 'only wallet creation remains skipped/fail-closed' when no KMS exists — true of one route, false of the value door. The consumer-facing 'Managed payment account: not ready' badge and the node's actual behaviour disagree.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes: the user is told their managed account is not ready, yet a tenant value action can still create and fund one under dev-grade custody. Invisible in the good case, misleading in the bad one.
findings.recommended: Move the custody-mode decision into WalletManager.GenerateWalletAsync (or a CustodyPolicy consulted by KeyCustodyService and WalletManager) so 'Disabled' fails closed at every wallet-creating path, and add a Production boot guard: CustodyMode must be Disabled or a registered adapter, never DevelopmentOnly.

findings.title: On live Algorand a freshly provisioned custodial wallet can never receive an asset — no opt-in, no min balance, and the provider's error names the ASA
findings.detail: AlgorandProvider refuses any transfer whose recipient has not opted in, with the message 'the account must sign its own opt-in — the platform cannot do it on its behalf' (:1017-1020; same for clawback :1425-1427). Neither EnsureWalletAsync nor TenantCustodialAccountManager funds the 0.1 ALGO minimum balance (+0.1 per ASA) a new account needs; NODE-HOST.md:368-374 only discusses gas for the platform signer. So in Live mode the first Transfer allocation to a 'Ready' user fails, and the failure string (ASA index, address, 'opt-in') flows straight back to ArdaNova as the error. findings.title: Who grants consent for a user ArdaNova provisioned but who never logs into AZOA?
findings.detail: The chokepoint fails closed on any tenant-driven SigningContext without a live ConsentGrant (KeyCustodyService.cs:119-127, :181-189). AllocationManager stamps ActingTenantId + SigningScope on the op when the caller acts as a tenant (:281-283, :335-336), so the check fires. But grants can only be created through ConsentController, which is [Authorize(Policy=FirstPartyLogin)] (:22-23, :39); TenantConsentController is GET/DELETE only (:24-25, :41, :70); ProvisionChildAsync creates no grant (TenantManager.cs:58-125); and child-credential issuance explicitly has 'NO OWNERSHIP-ONLY PATH' (:267-291). Two outcomes are possible and both are bad for the thesis: (a) ArdaNova's users must log into AZOA's first-party UI to consent — the user learns a second wallet-ish service exists; or (b) ArdaNova calls the value door with its plain tenant key so actingTenantId is null and the child user's key is signed with NO consent check at all. I did not trace how AllocationController derives actingTenantId from the API-key principal, so which branch ArdaNova actually hits is unverified.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes if (a): the user must visit AZOA to click 'allow'. Silently violates the self-sovereignty invariant if (b).
findings.recommended: Decide explicitly, then enforce: tenant-provisioned users get an implied, revocable grant scoped to the provisioning tenant, created inside ProvisionChildAsync and surfaced to the user inside ArdaNova's own settings (revocation via TenantConsentController DELETE). Add a test that a plain tenant-key allocation against a child user with no grant is refused.

Require first-party AZOA consent login (self-sovereign purity, thesis-hostile)

Finally, rotation covers only the per-user data KEK: the three per-chain platform secrets (AZOA:Algorand:PlatformMnemonic etc.) are plaintext config with no rotation tooling at all, and rotating the Algorand one means re-assigning ASA manager/reserve/clawback roles on every project token by hand.

findings.title: Being made implicitly: ArdaNova hosts its own AZOA node and therefore IS the custodian of record for its users
findings.detail: The integration contract §2 states custody follows the node operator: a self-hosted consumer node's operator 'custodies the keys of the users on it' (:90-98). ArdaNova's config binds a single Azoa:TenantId and a CustodyApiKey (AzoaSettings.cs:22-24, :77), and ValueApiKey/QuestApiKey are separated only in Production (:94-107). Nothing in either repo records whether ArdaNova will run the node (custodian, with money-transmitter/VASP exposure for a social-democrat community platform) or consume a shared node (no custody, but dependent on a third party's KMS). The runbook's KMS choice (D36 'vendor deferred', Railway has no native KMS) only makes sense under the self-hosted reading, and the user-self-sovereignty initiative (remove ArdaNova third-party custody) only makes sense under the shared reading. Whoever configures the first production node decides this.

findings.title: Custodial keypairs store no seed phrase, so KEK loss is unrecoverable and the rotation marker only proves a candidate key
findings.detail: GenerateCustodialKeypair persists EncryptedSeedPhrase = null by design (WalletManager.cs:416-428; onboarding doc :150-151), and AZOA stores no balances (chain is source of truth). If AZOA:WalletEncryptionKey is lost, every tenant-custodial wallet's funds are permanently inaccessible; the HIGH-1 marker (FilePendingRotationKeyStore) can only confirm that a key an operator still holds is the right one — it cannot recover a key nobody holds. No KEK backup/escrow procedure is documented in NODE-HOST.md. Conversely, if the KEK AND a DB read leak together, every custodial private key is exposed (single SHA-256 of one string protects them all). What a user loses if custody fails: the entire contents of their managed account, with no seed to recover it and no AZOA-side ledger to reconstruct a claim (ArdaNova's own intent/escrow records would be the only evidence).
findings.thesis_impact: Yes in the failure case: total loss, and the user never knew there was a key to lose.
findings.recommended: Before any real value: KEK in a secret manager with a second sealed copy; per-wallet random salt/DEK wrapped by the KEK (envelope encryption) so a KMS can later wrap the DEKs without re-keying users; document the recovery drill.

findings.title: What is the honest minimum custody posture for a first real-money milestone?
findings.detail: The owner rejected 'dev-grade config-derived custody for a first capped milestone' (D27 :425-429) and then, two weeks later, adopted an env-backed fallback as the interim mode while stating it does not clear D27 (D36 :637-647). Today's posture is therefore: AES-GCM under SHA-256(config string), per-chain plaintext platform mnemonics in env, no envelope encryption, no HSM, no signing-outage-free rotation, no hold primitive, no consent path for provisioned users, opt-in gap on live Algorand. The honest statement is that no real-money milestone is reachable without at least: (1) sign-only key handle + envelope encryption, (2) HOLD, (3) opt-in/min-balance funding, (4) bounded exposure (per-user and total float caps enforced in AllocationManager, not policy). Whether (1) must be a vendor HSM or an env-backed provider behind the sign-only handle with hard caps is the owner's call — D27 says HSM, D36 has quietly started building the other.

findings.recommended: Keep D27's bar for uncapped mainnet, but define a named 'capped pilot' posture the code can enforce: sign-only handle (env-backed provider allowed), envelope-encrypted DEKs, HOLD via platform holding wallet, per-user + total-float caps as AllocationManager invariants with tests, opt-in funding, dual-key rotation, volume-backed marker. Reconcile D27/D36 in the runbook so the next session does not re-litigate.

verticals.thesis_verdict: No. A non-crypto ArdaNova user cannot sponsor a project, escrow a bounty, or get paid for work today — and where the pipes do exist, the first live failure would teach them the word 'opt-in'. What is genuinely right: the custody layer is invisible and correctly shaped. KeyCustodyService is a single chokepoint that checks ownership and live consent BEFORE decrypting, hands the signer a byte[] that is zeroed in a finally, never logs or returns keys, and fails closed per chain with no cross-chain fallback; both dispatch seams enforce the same rail-capability and not-enabled gates; reconcile-before-retry is the correct branch table; rotation is idempotent with a loss-prevention marker; ArdaNova receives only public ids and never a secret, and its client copy says 'account setup' and 'managed payment account'. What is wrong is everything the thesis needs on top of that: (1) there is no HOLD anywhere, so escrow is unbuildable and ArdaNova's TaskEscrow can never be FUNDED; (2) the D36 'sign-without-export' seam does not exist — IPlatformKeyDerivation.TryDerive exports raw key bytes by contract and per-user keys sit under SHA-256 of one config string; (3) CustodyMode=Disabled only disables the tenant onboarding route while AllocationManager still mints config-KEK wallets; (4) on live Algorand a new custodial wallet cannot receive an asset (no opt-in, no min balance, OptInAsync has zero callers); (5) provisioned users have no consent-grant path that does not involve logging into AZOA; (6) parked payouts wait for a human; (7) ArdaNova's release dialog asks the sponsor for a tx hash and Settings offers Pera/WalletConnect. Honest minimum for a first real-money milestone: sign-only key handle with envelope-encrypted per-wallet DEKs (env-backed provider acceptable ONLY with enforced per-user and total-float caps in AllocationManager), a HOLD primitive on a platform holding wallet, custodial opt-in + min-balance funding, dual-key rotation on a volume-backed marker, and a real-value probe that actually reads CustodyMode. If custody fails under today's design a user loses the entire contents of a managed account they never knew had a key — no seed phrase is stored, AZOA keeps no balance ledger, and a leaked KEK plus a DB read exposes every custodial key at once.

findings.detail: A sponsor can see money IN (InvestorTable: opaque user id, USD, token units, protection badge) and a gate status, and nothing else. findings.thesis_impact: Every sponsor hits this on day one: they get a list of backers and a progress bar, never 'where did it go'.
findings.recommended: Build the ledger in ArdaNova from its own EconomicSettlement / ProjectInvestment / TaskEscrow / PayoutRequest rows with human descriptions and USD, and hang azoaOperationId off each row as a hidden 'verify' reference. Add an optional caller-supplied `Purpose` to AZOA AllocationRequest that lands in operation_log Parameters so the node-side record is self-describing too.

findings.title: Sponsor money never reaches AZOA — settlement gateway is a permanent Retry stub (in-flight, not landed)
findings.detail: After a verified Stripe webhook, FundingIntentService moves the intent to SETTLEMENT_PENDING and enqueues an outbox row; the dispatcher's only IAzoaSettlementGateway is DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway, which returns Retry('AZOA_SETTLEMENT_DISPATCH_DISABLED') forever. No code path assigns FundingIntentStatus.SETTLED (grep for '= FundingIntentStatus.SETTLED' is empty), and IAzoaAllocationService.AllocateFundingSettlementAsync has zero callers. The 'SETTLEMENT CONFIRMED' copy is therefore unreachable, and a sponsor's success page polls 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' indefinitely. Transparency consequence: there is no AZOA operation, receipt, or value stamp for any sponsor's money, so even a perfect ledger would have nothing node-side to reference. These files are in the ~81 uncommitted hardening set — describe as in-flight.
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: the first sponsorship ends in a spinner that never resolves.
findings.recommended: Treat 'live gateway + SETTLED transition + azoaOperationId surfaced to the sponsor' as one deliverable; do not ship a ledger UI ahead of it or it will be permanently empty.

findings.title: AZOA will never price, so USD presentation is ArdaNova's job — but nobody has claimed it
findings.detail: D16 is honest and consistent: IValueRateSource has no implementation, UnpricedValueRateSource is the default, Services/Analytics/AGENTS.md forbids implementing a rate source or back-filling, PositionSummary.UnrealizedValue is always null, and the operator frontend renders 'Unpriced' on every row. That is the right call for a neutral substrate and matches the thesis (ArdaNova owns valuation). The implicit decision nobody wrote down is that ArdaNova must therefore join its own USD figures (ProjectInvestment.usdAmount, PayoutRequest.usdAmount) to AZOA operation ids for any sponsor-readable number. ArdaNova's only analytics track (23-analytics-admin) is P3, admin-only, 0/8 items done, and product.md promises only 'Transparent Governance: On-chain decision making' — no sponsor-ledger promise exists in any spec on either repo.
findings.thesis_impact: Without the ArdaNova-side join, any surfaced AZOA figure is a base-unit integer with no currency.
options: ArdaNova owns the ledger and USD-at-settlement from its own tables; AZOA stays unpriced (recommended)
AZOA adds a tenant-supplied fiat stamp on AllocationRequest (caller-authoritative value at settlement) so operation_log carries USD without an oracle
Both: ArdaNova renders from its tables, AZOA stores the tenant-supplied stamp for audit re-derivation
findings.recommended: Option 3 is cheapest and most auditable: the tenant already decided the USD amount; letting it stamp value_* via a new 'TenantDeclared' RateSource keeps the D16 invariant (rate + source + timestamp stored, nothing fabricated by the node) while making ArdaNova rows re-derivable.

findings.title: AZOA analytics is structurally unreachable for ArdaNova end users, and speaks crypto when reached
findings.detail: Both /api/analytics routes take the subject exclusively from the credential (NameIdentifier/sub). ArdaNova's server calls AZOA with one tenant API key, whose NameIdentifier is the key OWNER, so the tenant cannot read any sponsor's history; the browser client is deliberately built with no apiKey and only reads wallets/portfolio/holons/run-state with the user's avatar JWT. No call to getAnalyticsTransactions/Positions exists in either ArdaNova tree. If it were wired, the payload is operationType/status/chainType/assetId/base-unit amount/txHash/fee — vocabulary the thesis says the user must never need. BlockchainOperationController's per-user route is likewise self-only (403 on mismatch).
findings.thesis_impact: Indirect today (nothing calls it); becomes direct the moment someone 'just shows the AZOA history' to sponsors.
findings.recommended: Do not expose AZOA analytics to sponsors. If ArdaNova needs node truth per user, add a tenant-scoped read behind acting-tenant consent (operation_log already has acting_tenant_id, OperationLog.cs:116) rather than loosening the self-scope.

findings.title: Sponsors and workers are already shown — and asked to type — raw transaction hashes

Each is a place a non-crypto user meets a chain artifact with no plain-language equivalent beside it.
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: a sponsor paying a worker via escrow is prompted for a tx hash.
findings.recommended: Make the reference optional-and-hidden (it already validates empty as valid, escrow-release.ts:12) and remove the input from the sponsor dialog entirely; render hashes only behind a 'Verify' disclosure.

findings.title: Should every signed-in viewer see individual backers' identities and amounts?

ProjectInvestmentDto also carries StripePaymentIntentId to that non-admin route. A social-democrat crowd wants to see where the money went, not necessarily who gave it; the current shape is neither anonymous nor named. Whether the client zod schema strips StripePaymentIntentId was not verified.
findings.thesis_impact: Privacy expectation of the audience; not a blocker.
options: Aggregate only (count + total) for non-members; itemised for the project team
Opt-in named backers, otherwise anonymous
Keep per-backer rows but show display name, not an internal id

findings.title: Node governance transparency is operator-level, disabled-by-default, and has no consumer — not a sponsor tool
findings.detail: The anonymous surface exposes allowlisted chains/asset types, the fee schedule, and treasury destination addresses plus their audit trails; nothing per-project or per-user. The signed history checkpoint is off by default (NodeTransparencyHistory.Enabled=false) so every response reports CryptographicHistoryProofAvailable=false. The SDK has no method for it, API_SYNC.md lists it as unmapped, and neither frontend calls it. tracks.md says 'landed; integrated verification remains' and plan item 7 is open — consistent, but the 'transparency' label invites the assumption that sponsor-facing transparency exists.
findings.thesis_impact: None directly; risk is misreporting it as user transparency.
findings.recommended: Rename in docs to 'node economic-rules transparency' and add one SDK read + an operator-console page so the surface at least has a consumer.

findings.title: Fee transparency exists in the data and nowhere in the UI

ArdaNova never surfaces a node fee to a sponsor or worker, and the outbox finalization keeps only OperationId/Receipt/Replayed. A backer who puts in $500 has no way to see that the node took a fee on the way through.

findings.recommended: Persist GrossAmount/NodeFeeAmount/NetAmount from the receipt onto EconomicSettlement and show 'platform fee' as a ledger line.

findings.title: Two arithmetic regimes: ArdaNova doubles vs AZOA decimal strings
findings.detail: PlatformTreasuryTransaction.amount and balanceAfter are double; ProjectInvestmentDto.UsdAmount is double; the client formats with Intl currency on number. AZOA refuses numbers everywhere (base-unit strings, minor-unit strings). Any future ledger that reconciles ArdaNova USD against AZOA amounts will drift by rounding, and 'no client-side arithmetic' is enforced only on the AZOA side.
findings.thesis_impact: Cents-level mismatches on a 'transparent' ledger destroy trust disproportionately.
findings.recommended: Move ArdaNova money columns to decimal(18,2)/minor-unit long before building the sponsor ledger.

Keep it as an operator-only tool
Ship it to users
