verticals.thesis_verdict: No. A sponsor today gets a Stripe checkout, a success page that polls 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' forever (the only AZOA settlement gateway is a disabled Retry stub, in-flight), and a Funding tab listing backers as 'User 3f9a…' with USD and 'token units'. They never see what the project spent, on what, or what fee was taken. The one plain-language ledger in the stack ('+$500.00 Funding Inflow — Index fund allocation from project X') is admin-only. AZOA's D16 analytics is honest and well-built but self-scoped to the credential subject (unreachable through ArdaNova's tenant key), permanently unpriced by design, and speaks base units / chain / asset id / tx hash — so 'just showing the node history' would be a thesis defect, not a fix. Meanwhile workers and sponsors are already shown raw tx hashes on escrow and credential pages, and a sponsor releasing escrow is prompted to type a 'transaction reference'. Node governance transparency and the conformance manifest are operator/machine surfaces with no consumer and no bearing on a sponsor's question. The plain-language ledger has no owner in any spec on either repo.

lens.verdict: Played as a schoolteacher, the journey is clean for exactly one step. Sign-up is Google-only and mentions nothing crypto (ardanova-client/src/server/auth/config.ts:236-253). Every later step either stops because a layer is absent or is fail-closed in production: (2) backing a project needs government-ID KYC plus a custodial Algorand wallet, and in production AZOA has no custody mode (CustodyMode "Disabled"; KmsHsm returns "No production KMS/HSM custody adapter is registered"), no KYC provider ("unavailable"), and ArdaNova's checkout readiness is structurally false because the only registered settlement gateway is DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway, which does not implement the capability interface the readiness check type-tests for; (3) a worker cannot even submit a bid from the client, escrow create/release/refund are 501/Failure, and AzoaAllocationService.AllocateRewardAsync has zero callers, so stake is never received; (4) voting is a fully rendered UI over a tRPC NOT_IMPLEMENTED and a backend 501, while README.md:89 still says Voting is "Complete"; (5) "where did the money go" has no non-admin layer — treasury is ADMIN-only, AZOA's anonymous node-transparency and allocation-receipt endpoints are consumed by nobody in ArdaNova. Before any of those stops, crypto concepts leak in five user-facing places a non-crypto user will hit: a global "Wallets" nav item leading to "Your Algorand public address"/PERA/DEFLY/mnemonic copy, the profile's custodial card rendering the Algorand wallet address and avatar GUID, the Credentials tab showing "ASA #", "Mint pending" and "Minted on Algorand" with transaction hashes, task rows saying "on-node settlement"/"allocation receipt", and the votes list printing "TX: <hash>". The largest implicit decision nobody has written down: a $50 sponsor and a first-time worker must both complete full KYC and hold a custodial chain wallet before any value moves — the thesis says they should not have to know that layer exists.

findings.title: Step 2 stops: funding checkout is structurally unreachable in production
findings.detail: FundingIntentService.CreateCheckoutAsync returns Conflict at line 71 whenever IFundingSettlementReadiness.IsReady is false. AzoaFundingSettlementReadiness.IsReady requires Azoa:EnableFundingCheckout (default false), a hosted outbox dispatcher (EnableSettlementOutboxWorker default false), AND `_gateway is ISelectedNodeSettlementCapability`. The only IAzoaSettlementGateway registered is DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway, and a repo-wide grep finds no class implementing ISelectedNodeSettlementCapability. So even if an operator flips both flags, IsReady is false by construction and every backer sees 'Funding checkout is unavailable until a selected AZOA node has enabled, attested settlement dispatch and reconciliation.' The DisabledAzoaSettlementGateway also returns Retry forever, so any settlement that did get recorded would poll 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' every 5s indefinitely (success/page.tsx:24-33, funding-intent-status.ts:26-31).
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the $50 backer reaches the Review step, clicks 'Create secure checkout', and is told funding is unavailable. No Stripe page ever opens.
findings.recommended: Implement a real IAzoaSettlementGateway that also implements ISelectedNodeSettlementCapability (attested node id, CanDispatch/CanReconcile), register it behind Azoa:EnableFundingCheckout, and add a test that fails if IsReady can never be true with the registered gateway type.

findings.title: AZOA has no production custody mode, so walletReady is never true outside Development
findings.detail: TenantCustodialAccountManager.BuildCapabilities computes custodyAvailable only when CustodyMode == DevelopmentOnly AND IsDevelopment AND Blockchain:Mode == Simulated AND a >=32-char wallet key exists. Production appsettings ships CustodyMode 'Disabled'; the KmsHsm branch returns 'No production KMS/HSM custody adapter is registered.' ArdaNova's isValueActionAccountReady (client) and AzoaValueEligibilityService.RequireReadyAsync (backend, uncommitted) both require walletReady, so in production every value action — fund, accept paid work, receive funding — fails closed with 'Complete account setup' and the user has no way to complete it.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the profile card shows 'Managed payment account: Not created' forever and 'Start account setup' cannot succeed.
findings.recommended: Decide the production custody adapter (KMS/HSM per DEPLOY-STEPS B3) before any ArdaNova value feature is described as available; surface the unavailableReason verbatim in the ArdaNova card so operators can see which leg is missing.

findings.title: Which KYC vendor, and who pays — production has none
findings.detail: AZOA production config sets Kyc:Provider 'unavailable'. KycManager refuses any hosted provider that does not implement IHostedSessionProvider; only IdentomatKycProviderService does (Veriff and GenericHosted are fail-closed stubs). ManualKycProviderService is HostedVerification=false and expects document references, which ArdaNova's AGENTS.md explicitly refuses to collect. ArdaNova's verification page computes canStart = identityReady && kycReady && (hostedVerification || developmentSimulation), so with the shipped config the 'Identity verification' button never enables.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the backer is sent to /settings/verification and finds a disabled flow with 'Provider selected by node operator'.
options: Identomat (only adapter that implements the hosted seam today)
Veriff (adapter exists but is a refused stub — needs the seam implemented)
Manual review via AZOA operator console (requires ArdaNova to build a private upload path it currently refuses to build)
findings.recommended: Pick Identomat for the first tenant since it is the only seam-complete adapter; treat Veriff as a follow-up track.

findings.title: Implicit decision: a $50 sponsor and a first-time worker must pass government-ID KYC and hold a custodial chain wallet before any value moves
findings.detail: There is no amount threshold anywhere. The invest page hides checkout behind isValueActionAccountReady (identity + KYC Approved + wallet id + wallet address), the backend repeats it for funder AND recipient at checkout time, and TaskCommerceService requires both project owner and contributor to be fully ready before a bid can be accepted. Nobody has written down that KYC-before-$50 is the product policy; it fell out of AZOA's 'gate at the value seams' contract decision (§11.4) being applied uniformly. For a social-democrat audience this is the single largest friction against the thesis, and it is a policy choice, not a plumbing constraint.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — this is the first moment the user learns there is a regulated identity + custody layer under a $50 pledge.
options: KYC for everyone before any value action (current)
Tiered: no KYC below a fiat threshold with off-chain ledger only; KYC at payout/withdrawal
KYC only for recipients of value (owners/workers), not for sponsors paying by card
findings.recommended: Tiered. Sponsors paying by Stripe card under a threshold should not need KYC; gate KYC at the point value leaves the platform (payout) and at worker acceptance. Record it in conductor/product.md so the gate stops being implicit.

findings.title: Step 3 stops at the first click: a worker cannot submit a bid from the client
findings.detail: Paid work runs through OpportunityBid (TaskCommerceService.AcceptBidAsync requires a bid with proposedAmount). The tRPC router opportunityBid.create and the HTTP endpoint POST /api/opportunity-bids both exist, but no page or component calls them — the only worker-side mutation is opportunity.submitApplication, which creates an Application, not a Bid. OpportunityBidsPanel and BidAcceptButton are owner-only. So the schoolteacher can apply but can never be 'accepted' into a paid assignment.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the layer is absent on the client. Nothing crypto is exposed because nothing happens.
findings.recommended: Either add a worker-side 'Propose terms' form that calls opportunityBid.create, or make AcceptBid accept an Application with an owner-entered award so the existing apply flow is the paid path.

findings.title: Step 3 stops again: escrow and reward allocation are 501/Failure and the allocation service has no callers
findings.detail: Accepting a bid creates a TaskCommerceAgreement with escrowStatus NONE. From there: TaskEscrowsController POST returns 501; TaskEscrowService.ReleaseAsync and RefundAsync return a fixed Failure; AzoaAllocationService.AllocateRewardAsync (the POST /api/allocation/{userId} client) is registered in DI and referenced by nothing else. The commerce page truthfully says 'Funding, escrow, quest linking, release approval, and AZOA settlement are separate gated steps.' The worker therefore never receives stake. tracks.md is accurate here ('no production trigger dispatches it yet') but README.md:109 still lists 'Task Marketplace ... escrow' as a Q2 2025 deliverable.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — flow stops; the worker sees 'units are reserved in the agreement' and nothing else ever happens.

findings.title: Step 4 stops: voting UI is fully rendered over a NOT_IMPLEMENTED tRPC and a 501 backend
findings.detail: overview-tab.tsx renders vote options, a reason textarea and 'Submit Vote'; governanceRouter.vote is bound to governanceMutationsUnavailable() which throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED; the backend POST proposals/{id}/vote returns 501 'Actor-bound proposal, vote, and comment authority plus auditable atomic lifecycle transitions are required'. The client surfaces it as window.alert(error.message). README.md:89 claims 'Community Support: Voting ... Complete' — stale.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the user builds a vote, submits, and gets a browser alert with engineering jargon.
findings.recommended: Hide or disable the vote form with plain-language copy until the governance track closes; fix README.md:89.

findings.title: When the vote 501 is lifted, vote weight and voter identity are caller-supplied
findings.detail: GovernanceService.CastVoteAsync stores voterId = dto.VoterId and weight = dto.Weight ?? 1 straight from the request body. The 501 gate is the only thing preventing a vote-weight injection and voting-as-someone-else. AZOA's own governance nodes are blocked for a related reason (tally reads raw holons — Sybil hole) per NotEnabledActionNodeTypes. Nothing in ArdaNova defines what a vote-of-record even is (one person, one credential, token-weighted).
findings.thesis_impact: Not yet reachable, but the first governance release would ship it.
options: One member, one vote, bound to the authenticated actor
Membership-credential-gated (requires the Algorand ASA credential — exposes crypto to voters)
Token-weighted (contradicts README's 'project token does not imply voting rights')
findings.recommended: One authenticated member, one vote; derive weight server-side; never accept VoterId/Weight from the body.

findings.title: Step 5 has no user-facing layer: 'where did the money go' is admin-only, and AZOA's transparency endpoints are consumed by nobody
findings.detail: A backer can see: their Portfolio token balance records ('A token balance is not proof of equity...'), the project's 'Current funding $X of $Y' bar, and an InvestorTable of other backers. There is no per-project ledger of inflows/outflows. TreasuryController data is only rendered on /admin/treasury, guarded by session.user.role === 'ADMIN', with copy about syncing 'on-chain and off-chain'. AZOA exposes anonymous GET /api/node-transparency/audit/treasury and the allocation receipt/reconcile routes, but a grep of ArdaNova (backend + client) finds zero references to either.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — 'transparent settlement' is the thesis promise and the user has no screen for it.
findings.recommended: Add a per-project 'Money' view fed by EconomicSettlement rows (funding in, awards out, protection paid) in plain language; optionally link AZOA allocation receipts as 'proof' without showing hashes.

findings.title: Global 'Wallets' nav item drops every user into the full crypto vocabulary two clicks after sign-up
findings.detail: app-sidebar utilityItems puts 'Wallets' next to 'Settings' for every authenticated user. /settings/wallets offers providers PERA/DEFLY/ALGOSIGNER/WALLETCONNECT, an input labelled 'Your Algorand public address', and the copy 'ArdaNova never asks for a private key, mnemonic, or custody access' and 'requires a one-time signed proof through a supported browser wallet'. /settings/payouts ('Payouts are safely disabled') has exactly one CTA: 'MANAGE EXTERNAL WALLETS'. For the schoolteacher this is the first sighting of wallet, Algorand, address, mnemonic, private key and signature — none of which the thesis wants them to learn.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — reachable from every page.
findings.recommended: Remove 'Wallets' from the default nav; expose external-wallet linking only behind an opt-in 'Advanced' setting for users who already hold one.

findings.title: The profile's account-setup card renders the Algorand wallet address and the AZOA avatar GUID
findings.detail: CustodialAccountCard shows step 03 'Managed payment account' with compactReference(status.walletAddress) — the first 10 and last 8 characters of an Algorand address — and step 01 'Account setup' with the raw avatar GUID. ArdaNova persists walletAddress on User.azoaWalletAddress and returns it in the status DTO on purpose. The label is friendly but the artifact is a chain address, and it sits on /dashboard/profile for every user.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the first crypto artifact a non-crypto user sees, on their own profile.
findings.recommended: Render 'Ready' / 'Not created' only; keep the address server-side (it is never needed by the user).

findings.title: Credentials surface says 'ASA #', 'Mint pending', 'Minted on Algorand' and prints transaction hashes
findings.detail: The profile Credentials tab uses CredentialCard, which shows a MintStatusIndicator ('Mint pending' / 'Mint reference recorded') and 'ASA #{assetId}'. The credential detail page has a 'Blockchain Status' block: 'Minted on Algorand', 'This credential is verified on the Algorand blockchain', 'Chain Verified', and full 'Mint Transaction' / revoke hashes. Membership credentials are the thing the thesis calls 'portable credentials' — this is where the benefit is delivered wrapped in the vocabulary the thesis forbids. The README also carries an 'Algorand-ASA' badge.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — reachable from 'Join a project or guild to earn one!' on the profile.
findings.recommended: Replace with 'Verified' / 'Verification pending' and a 'View proof' disclosure for the curious.

findings.title: Task rows and commerce states use settlement jargon: 'on-node settlement', 'allocation receipt', 'ALLOCATION ESCROWED'
findings.detail: TaskEconomicState labels (ALLOCATION UNFUNDED / ESCROWED / SETTLEMENT PENDING / DISPUTED / RETURNED) and details such as 'Do not treat this as an on-node settlement until the allocation receipt is recorded' render on every task card that has a reward, on /tasks and /dashboard/tasks. The commerce page adds 'quest linking' and 'AZOA settlement'.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the worker's task list.

findings.title: Dead escrow UI asks a human to paste a 'Chain hash or operation ID', and escrow funding evidence is a client-supplied tx hash
findings.detail: ReleaseDialog's only input is 'Chain hash or operation ID' with help text 'Provide the chain hash or operation ID recorded for this release.' EscrowDetailCard renders txHashFund/txHashRelease. Neither is mounted today (only admin/disputes imports escrow components), but the backend model already accepts CreateTaskEscrowDto.TxHashFund from the caller. The implicit decision being coded is that escrow proof is a user-typed hash rather than a server-observed settlement.
findings.thesis_impact: Not today (unmounted); would be the moment a project owner has to learn what a tx hash is.
findings.recommended: Delete the hash input; escrow release evidence must come from the settlement outbox/receipt, never from a form field.

findings.title: Votes list prints 'TX: <hash>' and Vote is modelled with txHash
findings.detail: votes-tab.tsx renders `TX: {vote.txHash.slice(0,10)}...{vote.txHash.slice(-8)}` whenever a vote carries a hash. Combined with the vote-of-record question this bakes in the assumption that a vote is an on-chain transaction the voter can see.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes once voting is enabled.

findings.title: No self-serve path to make a project fundable: token config is AdminApiKey-only and needs an Algorand asset id nobody in ArdaNova sets
findings.detail: POST /api/projecttokens/config and all allocate/gate routes require AuthorizationPolicies.AdminApiKey; no client page calls projectTokens.createConfig. FundingIntentService refuses checkout unless config.assetId is non-empty ('requires a verified asset id before funding checkout'), and a grep shows no ArdaNova code path ever assigns ProjectTokenConfig.assetId (only reads). So the project creator's 'Funding' tab says 'Funding is not configured' until an operator creates an ASA by hand and writes the row. The creator is shielded from crypto only because they are shielded from the feature.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — the local project the teacher wants to back is not fundable unless an operator intervened.
findings.recommended: A publish-time server job (not the creator) creates the project token via AZOA fungible-mint and writes assetId; the creator only sets human terms (name, supply, disclosure).

findings.title: Every signed-in user can see every backer's user id and USD amount on a project's Funding tab
findings.detail: InvestorTable lists 'User {shortReference(userId)}' with title={userId}, USD amount and token amount. The tRPC procedure is protectedProcedure (any signed-in user); the backend GET /api/projecttokens/{configId}/investors has no [Authorize] attribute at class or method level. A social platform for a social-democrat audience will get asked why a $50 pledge is visible to strangers.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes — on step 5 the teacher sees other people's pledges and vice versa.
options: Public by design (transparency) with explicit consent at checkout
Visible to project members only
Aggregate totals only for non-members
findings.recommended: Aggregate for non-members; named only with a per-pledge 'show my name' consent captured at checkout.

findings.title: A verified card payment can sit in settlement limbo because of someone else's KYC
findings.detail: RecordPaymentSucceededAsync (Stripe webhook) records the settlement with failureCode AZOA_PROJECT_OWNER_NOT_READY when the project owner's AZOA readiness lapses between checkout and webhook. The backer's money has been captured by Stripe; the success page polls 'SETTLEMENT PENDING' and there is no refund or cancel action on it. The pre-checkout recipient check (lines 101-106) reduces but does not close the window.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes when funding goes live — the backer is told nothing they can act on.

findings.title: Custodial recipients of project tokens need an Algorand opt-in and minimum balance that nothing in the allocation path provisions
findings.detail: AlgorandProvider refuses any ASA transfer to an account that has not opted in and states the account must sign its own opt-in. AllocationManager.MintAsync/EnsureWalletAsync generate a wallet and mint, but the mint path shown contains no opt-in call, and no code funds the recipient's ALGO minimum balance (0.1 ALGO per ASA). For a custodial wallet AZOA holds the key and could sign the opt-in, but someone must pay the MBR. Whoever hits this first will explain 'gas'/'min balance' to the user.
findings.thesis_impact: Yes at the first real allocation to a worker.
options: Platform treasury pays opt-in + MBR for every custodial wallet at provisioning
Opt-in lazily on first allocation, funded by the tenant
Keep balances off-chain in AZOA's ledger and only settle on-chain at withdrawal
findings.recommended: Platform-funded opt-in inside AllocationManager.EnsureWalletAsync so the user never learns the concept.

findings.title: No onboarding: nothing after Google sign-in points the user to account setup, and the setup card is buried on the profile page
findings.detail: Sign-in creates the Prisma user (role INDIVIDUAL, VOLUNTEER) and lands on the dashboard, which has no verification/account-setup prompt. The CustodialAccountCard lives on /dashboard/profile and /settings/verification; the user discovers it only when the invest page or bid-accept button bounces them with 'Complete account setup'. Track 17 (Onboarding) is unstarted.
findings.thesis_impact: Moderate — the friction is discovered at the moment of generosity.

findings.title: Stale status and terminology drift the next engineer will trust

Complete' vs 501; README roadmap rows dated 2025 for features that are 501 today; README badge 'Algorand-ASA' contradicts the product framing; tracks.md marks azoa-user-onboarding 'Largely shipped' while Azoa:EnableCustodialAccounts defaults false (DisabledAzoaCustodialAccountGateway is registered) and AZOA has no production custody. The in-flight eligibility gate (IAzoaValueEligibilityService) is untracked and referenced by seven tracked files — the RUNBOOK's own warning that `git commit -a` produces a non-building tree still stands.

findings.title: The invest flow already frames a pledge as buying '% of supply' in project tokens; the browser never touches azoa-sdk
findings.detail: The Review step shows formatToken(sourceTokenAmount, unitName), an 'Informational ARDA equivalent', and formatPct(share of totalSupply); Stripe's line item is 'Fund Project: {AssetName}'. This is thesis-compatible (internal token economy) but 'share of total supply' is a crypto framing, and QUICK_AMOUNTS start at $100 so a $50 backer types the amount. Positive: azoa-sdk is imported nowhere in the client's app code, so the SDK's wallet/chain vocabulary never reaches the browser.
findings.thesis_impact: Low — vocabulary only.
options: Keep supply-% framing
Show 'your share of this project's support' in plain terms and hide supply math behind a disclosure
findings.recommended: Plain-terms framing; keep the number available in the disclosure.

lens.verdict: The thesis ("benefits of blockchain without knowing blockchain") is achievable, but the two repos are currently building it in the inverted order. Everything a thesis user actually touches — sponsor a project with a card, get paid in USD, hold a membership badge — is disabled, gated, or half-built in two places at once (ArdaNova PayoutService.ProcessPayoutAsync hard-returns failure; AZOA has no fiat rail provider; Stripe Connect code exists only in ArdaNova; every value action requires hosted Identomat KYC first). Everything the thesis says must be invisible — three chains, a bridge, a wallet-provider picker (PERA/DEFLY/WalletConnect), a seed-phrase export dialog, on-chain ASA minting per reward — is built and reachable. Of the six structural tensions examined, two are product-solvable without an owner decision (ASA spendability via internal-ledger-first; KYC tiering for sponsors), three need the owner to pick a side because both sides are partially coded (custody model: the contract still says "self-sovereign" while the shipped ArdaNova path provisions tenant-owned child users who can never export; off-ramp owner: ArdaNova Stripe Connect vs AZOA fiat rail; chargeback resolution: platform clawback vs hold-until-window vs absorb — and clawback quietly weakens "real ownership"), and one is a compliance question that no code in either repo addresses (tax at receipt of equity tokens for work; D16 pushes it to the consumer and the consumer has zero tax code). The most consequential implicit DECISION is chain-first/fiat-last (D27 gates Phase 3 fiat behind KMS custody; D26 ships ETH/Solana/bridge that neither consumer needs), which means the "get paid for work" promise ships last. Real-value risk today is nil only because three independent kill-switches are all off (AZOA CustodyMode=Disabled, RealValueEnabled=false, ArdaNova Algorand:Provider=Simulated); the money-printers identified below (card dispute after irreversible mint, no ASA opt-in path for custodial recipients, no min-balance funding) are latent, not fixed.

findings.title: Build order is chain-first, fiat-last — the thesis user's two core moments ship last
findings.detail: RUNBOOK §1 scopes six workstreams; the two that matter to a non-crypto user — fiat sponsorship and USD payout (item 5) — are 'Open, gated on custody' behind D27 (KMS/HSM before any Phase 3 fiat step) and D36 (vendor deferred, env-backed fallback explicitly does NOT clear D27). Meanwhile D26 records the owner directing Ethereum, Solana SPL and a cross-chain bridge to ship 'against the evidence' that neither consumer needs them. On the consumer side, ArdaNova's PayoutService.ProcessPayoutAsync is a hard-coded failure ('Payout processing is disabled until a verified provider transfer and durable settlement reconciliation are available') and the /settings/payouts page tells users payouts are 'safely disabled'. Net effect: a worker can be assigned a paid task (after KYC), have an NFT-holon minted into a custodial wallet, and have no path to money. The thesis would invert this: internal ledger + Stripe (in and out) first, chain as an audit anchor later.
options: A. Keep chain-first: finish KMS custody (D27), then AZOA fiat rail (D7/D9/D11), then payouts — thesis moments ship last

B. Fiat-first: ArdaNova owns Stripe in+out via Connect (code already at StripeService.cs:290-380), rewards live in ArdaNova's Postgres TokenBalanceService until liquid, AZOA chain mint becomes a later 'anchor' step behind the same idempotency key
C. Hybrid: keep AZOA as ledger-of-record (operation_log) but with a Fiat.USD IValueRailProvider whose TransferAsync delegates to Stripe Connect; chain rails stay disabled until custody lands
findings.recommended: B now, C when D27 clears — B is the only order in which a real user can sponsor and get paid before KMS procurement finishes
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: the sponsor→worker→payout loop is the product; today it dead-ends at a disabled payout page

findings.title: Self-sovereign custody vs invisibility is already resolved de facto as CUSTODIAL — but the docs still promise sovereignty
findings.detail: The contract (§2) and ArdaNova track copy say users are 'first-class self-sovereign identities'. The shipped path is the opposite: ArdaNova calls PUT /api/tenant/custodial-accounts/{externalSubject}, which provisions a tenant-OWNED child user (ProvisionChildModel { ExternalUserId }) and a platform wallet whose key is AES-wrapped under the node's config key (KeyCustodyService). AZOA's only key-export surface is WalletController.Export, gated by the RecentFirstPartyLogin policy — a tenant-provisioned child user has no first-party login, so an ArdaNova user can never take their keys out. That is a legitimate product choice (and the only one compatible with 'never learn a seed phrase'), but it must be stated: 'real ownership' here means ownership-of-record in a custodian's ledger, and the ArdaNova onboarding spec's 'Locked decisions: self-register + self-run, no fleet map, no tenant:provision' is false against the code.

options: A. Declare custodial: strip 'self-sovereign' from contract §2, tracks.md Phase E and product copy; keep export off for tenant children
B. Custodial-by-default with a later 'claim your keys' upgrade: requires a first-party credential for child users plus an export/ownership-transfer rail (not designed anywhere)
C. Non-custodial via passkey/MPC signing (user never sees a seed, node never holds a full key) — a new custody workstream replacing D27's KMS direction
findings.recommended: A immediately (it is what the code does), with B recorded as future-state so the sovereignty claim is not silently lost
findings.thesis_impact: Structural: the thesis's 'real ownership' benefit is only true in the custodial sense unless B or C is built

findings.title: KYC is required for ANY value action, including a $5 sponsorship, an equity-bearing job listing, and a membership badge
findings.detail: AZOA's KycGateService has no amount threshold: identity Approved AND AML NO_HIT or the gate is closed, for every value move. ArdaNova's in-flight AzoaValueEligibilityService.IsReadyForValueAction additionally requires KycStatus==Approved && WalletReady && WalletAddress, and it is called before: funding a project (funder AND recipient), creating/updating a paid task (actor AND assignee), posting an opportunity with any compensation or equityPercent>0, accepting a bid, and issuing a membership credential (RequireProAsync). A sponsor therefore must complete a hosted Identomat document-verification session — a compliance flow the thesis says they should never see — before putting $5 on a card. Identity KYC can be tiered by amount as a product choice; sanctions screening (D24) generally cannot, so the honest floor is 'lightweight screening for everyone, document KYC only when liquidating'.
options: A. KYC-for-all before any value (current) — simplest compliance story, worst conversion

B. Tiered: sponsors below a cumulative de-minimis pay via Stripe with no AZOA KYC (Stripe carries cardholder risk); document KYC required only to RECEIVE value or cash out; AML screen everyone cheaply
C. Recipient-only: never KYC sponsors; KYC workers/founders at first payout request
findings.recommended: B, with counsel — it keeps the sponsor path crypto- and compliance-free and moves the friction to the one moment (payout) where the user already expects paperwork
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: the 'ask the community for sponsorship' moment currently opens with a passport upload

findings.title: Card dispute after an irreversible mint has no handler in either repo — D10's reversal pipeline is a decision, not code
findings.detail: ArdaNova's Stripe webhook dispatches only payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.payment_failed / transfer.reversed / transfer.updated / transfer.created. There is no charge.dispute.created, charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn, or charge.refunded case. AZOA's SDK stripe orchestration still returns {status:'ignored'} for every event except checkout.session.completed — the exact defect D10 names as 'silently discarded'. On payment success ArdaNova calls the AZOA allocation with Kind=Mint, which mints an NFT-holon on chain into the recipient's custodial wallet. A day-60 dispute therefore removes the USD from the Stripe balance while the minted asset and ArdaNova's Postgres token balance remain. SettlementProfile.TryGetReleaseTimeUtc exists but I found no caller consuming it on the allocation path (not exhaustively verified). Latent only because RealValueEnabled=false, CustodyMode=Disabled and ArdaNova Algorand:Provider=Simulated.

options: A. Platform absorbs disputes from a treasury reserve (simplest; needs a reserve policy and D16-style facts to size it)
B. Hold: rewards/allocations stay frozen (ArdaNova holderClass gate or ASA defaultFrozen) until SettlementProfile.ReversalWindow elapses, then release

C. Clawback: on dispute, AZOA uses the ASA clawback address it already sets to pull the asset back — technically cheap on Algorand, but it means the platform can seize any asset it issued, which qualifies 'real ownership'
findings.recommended: B for the window plus C as the exceptional path, and say so in user-facing terms ('rewards become yours after N days')
findings.thesis_impact: Structural: irreversible chain settlement vs reversible card money is not cosmetic; whichever option is chosen changes what 'ownership' means to the user

findings.title: A worker cannot receive an existing ASA into a fresh custodial wallet: no code path ever signs the recipient's opt-in, and nothing funds the Algorand minimum balance
findings.detail: AlgorandProvider refuses any ASA transfer to an address that has not opted in ('the account must sign its own opt-in — the platform cannot do it on its behalf'). IBlockchainProviderModule declares OptInAsync, but no Manager, Service or Controller calls it. So AllocationKind.Transfer (ArdaNova uses it at AzoaAllocationService.cs:119) into a wallet that AllocationManager.EnsureWalletAsync just generated will fail closed at the provider. Only Kind=Mint-a-new-asset-per-reward works (the creator is auto-opted-in), which is what rewards use — but minting from the user's own wallet needs the wallet to hold ALGO for the fee and the 0.1 ALGO per-asset minimum balance, and the only funding path is a faucet that WalletManager disables on mainnet. The RUNBOOK's own 'Outstanding, unscheduled' list confirms 'operator funding / treasury ... fee-payer balances ... appear nowhere'. The thesis needs gas and opt-ins to be invisible; today they are unhandled, not hidden.
findings.evidence: c:\Users\atooz\Programming\Projects\oasis-sleek\Providers\Blockchain\Algorand\AlgorandProvider.cs:1016-1020,1410-1430; Interfaces\IBlockchainProviderModule.cs:39 (only declaration; grep of Managers/Services/Controllers finds no caller); Managers\AllocationManager.cs:143,215-235,294-345; Managers\WalletManager.cs:567; conductor\RUNBOOK.md ('Outstanding, unscheduled' → 'Operator funding / treasury'); ardanova ...\AzoaAllocationService.cs:63,92,119
options: A. Internal-ledger-first: rewards are rows in ArdaNova/AZOA, chain minting is an anchor the user never depends on — opt-in/min-balance become an operator batch concern

B. Platform-sponsored chain: AZOA auto-signs opt-ins for custodial wallets via KeyCustodyService (it holds the key), and a node fee-payer account funds min balance — needs the treasury workstream the runbook says does not exist
C. Single pooled custodial account with sub-ledger (no per-user chain wallets at all) — cheapest, weakest 'ownership' story
findings.recommended: A now; B when the treasury/fee-payer workstream is scoped
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: 'get paid for work' fails at the chain boundary for any Transfer allocation; Mint allocations fail on an unfunded wallet

findings.title: Off-ramp ownership is split: ArdaNova has Stripe Connect code, AZOA has the fiat-rail seam, neither is wired to a payout
findings.detail: ArdaNova's StripeService already implements Connect Express onboarding (CreateConnectedAccountAsync with account_onboarding links) and CreatePayoutTransferAsync, and its webhook handles transfer.reversed/updated. AZOA's D7/D9/D11 direction is a Fiat.USD IValueRailProvider reached only through fiat-sidecar — but no such provider exists (only the interface and tests reference the seam) and fiat-sidecar exposes a single inbound /api/checkout route. The contract §1 assigns 'webhook signature verification (fiat/payment provider)' to the consumer, which points toward ArdaNova owning fiat. Two half-builds pointing different ways is an implicit decision waiting to be made by whoever codes next. Note Stripe Connect Express onboarding is itself a second compliance flow (bank details, tax ID) the worker will see on top of Identomat.

options: A. ArdaNova owns fiat end-to-end (Stripe Checkout in, Connect out); AZOA never touches USD; D7/D9/D11 fiat scope is retired to 'ledger facts only'
B. AZOA owns fiat as a rail (finish Fiat.USD provider + sidecar payout route + D10 reversal saga); ArdaNova deletes its Connect code
C. Split by direction: consumer collects (Checkout), AZOA pays out (rail) — worst option, two Stripe accounts and two webhook secrets
findings.recommended: A — it matches contract §1, reuses code that already exists, and keeps Stripe secrets out of the node
findings.thesis_impact: Direct: 'get paid' in USD is impossible until one side is chosen

findings.title: Tax at receipt of equity tokens for work: D16 pushes it to the consumer, and the consumer has zero tax code
findings.detail: D16 and RUNBOOK §1 pin AZOA as 'finance-focused, not tax/regulator-focused': it exposes facts, consumers compute tax. AZOA's analytics are unpriced by design (IValueRateSource has only UnpricedValueRateSource; Services/Analytics/AGENTS.md forbids back-filling). ArdaNova has no occurrence of 'tax', '1099' or 'taxable' in client, backend or conductor. Yet ArdaNova DOES have a price source — ExchangeService's treasury-backed deterministic rate, used at PayoutService.cs:93-97 — and never stamps it into the allocation memo/metadata that reaches operation_log. In most jurisdictions, property received for services is income at fair value on receipt; a worker earning equity ASAs will owe tax on tokens they cannot sell (payouts disabled). The thesis's audience will meet this as a surprise letter, not a screen.

options: A. Stamp USD-at-receipt from ArdaNova's ExchangeService into the allocation and issue annual statements from AZOA's D16 analytics — requires an IValueRateSource that AZOA's own AGENTS.md currently forbids implementing

B. Restricted-until-liquid: rewards are non-transferable/unvested (ArdaNova's holderClass + gate model already does this) so the taxable event is deferred to payout — invisible to the user, but needs counsel to confirm treatment
C. Disclaim and leave to the user
findings.recommended: B with counsel; it is the only option that keeps the user from learning a crypto-tax concept before they see cash
findings.thesis_impact: Structural: token compensation is taxable in a way cash is not; ignoring it converts a benefit into a liability for the audience

findings.title: ArdaNova ships a raw crypto wallet page (PERA/DEFLY/ALGOSIGNER/WALLETCONNECT + paste-an-address + sign-a-challenge) in the sidebar of every user
findings.detail: /settings/wallets asks the user to pick a wallet provider from ['PERA','DEFLY','ALGOSIGNER','WALLETCONNECT','OTHER'], paste an Algorand address, and (via WalletVerificationService) sign a challenge. It is linked from the app sidebar and from the disabled payouts page ('MANAGE EXTERNAL WALLETS'). No backend service depends on a primary external wallet (grep for primaryWallet/isPrimary outside WalletServices is empty), so this is dead weight that exposes exactly the concepts the thesis forbids. There is even a QA checklist variant named '...NO-WALLET' acknowledging the split.
findings.recommended: Remove the route and sidebar entry until a 'claim to external wallet' feature is actually designed (see custody question option B)

findings.title: D9's 'fiat-only persona who should never see a blockchain' cannot exist in ArdaNova — every value action requires an Algorand wallet address
findings.detail: D9 explicitly names the persona ('a fiat-only Taawun congregant — exactly the persona who should never see a blockchain') and makes ChainCapabilityGate rail-aware so they pass a fiat payout. ArdaNova's in-flight readiness check goes the other way: IsReadyForValueAction demands WalletReady && WalletId && WalletAddress in addition to KYC. A user whose entire journey is card-in / Connect-out still gets an Algorand keypair generated and shown (truncated) on the account card. The consumer gate is stricter than the substrate's own intent.
findings.recommended: Make wallet readiness rail-specific in ArdaNova (fiat actions require KYC only), mirroring D9
findings.thesis_impact: A card-only sponsor is forced through wallet provisioning they never use

findings.title: D19/D41 clawback-based revocation quietly makes the platform able to seize any asset it issued — 'real ownership' is conditional
findings.detail: D19 chooses Algorand's native clawback for soulbound revocation and notes the codebase 'already sets' the clawback address on ASAs it creates. Clawback is an asset-level parameter: whichever account holds it can move that ASA out of ANY holder at any time, credential or not. If FungibleTokenManager sets clawback on every ASA (not only soulbound ones — I did not verify the branch), then equity/reward tokens are seizable by the node operator, which is a materially different 'ownership' promise than the thesis makes. This is also the lever that makes the chargeback option C cheap — the two decisions are coupled and should be made together.
options: A. Clawback only on soulbound credentials; equity/reward ASAs minted with clawback=zero-address (truly non-seizable, no dispute lever)
B. Clawback on all platform-issued ASAs, disclosed as 'platform may reverse rewards for fraud/chargeback' — matches a custodial model honestly
findings.recommended: Decide jointly with the chargeback question; whichever is chosen, state it in user terms
findings.thesis_impact: Structural: the meaning of 'you own it' depends on this parameter

findings.title: Sybil protection is opt-in per operation (D3) and only GovernanceVoteNodeHandler opts in — allocation, funding and per-person quotas do not
findings.detail: D1/D23 allow many verified avatars per person and make uniqueness a per-operation opt-in. The only consumer of IPersonUniquenessGate is GovernanceVoteNodeHandler (grep). The RUNBOOK's adversarial note on D1 warns that 'any new value operation that implicitly assumes one-avatar-per-human is now wrong by default'. AllocationManager and ArdaNova reward/funding paths do not declare a uniqueness requirement, so per-person caps ArdaNova may add later (e.g. one founder credential per person, sponsor match limits) will be multiplied by re-verification under a second avatar. Not thesis-conflicting; it is the residual risk the runbook already accepts, surfaced so ArdaNova does not assume it is protected.
